posts.contentHtml:
Bay Mau Coconut Forest, a green gem nestled in the heart of Hoi An, is a must-visit destination renowned for its unspoiled natural beauty and unique river-based cultural experiences. This article provides detailed and up-to-date information on basket boat ticket prices for 2026, highlights exciting activities, and shares essential travel tips to help you enjoy a truly memorable visit.

Bay Mau Coconut Forest is a lush green oasis hidden within the tranquil countryside of Hoi An. With endless rows of water coconut palms stretching along winding waterways, this destination offers visitors a peaceful escape and an authentic glimpse into traditional rural life in Central Vietnam. Drifting gently along narrow canals in a traditional basket boat while immersing yourself in the cool, green surroundings is an experience not to be missed. So, how much does a basket boat ride cost in 2026, and what should you know to make the most of your trip? Let us explore Bay Mau Coconut Forest in detail.

Where Is Bay Mau Coconut Forest And How To Get There?

Bay Mau Coconut Forest is located in Cam Thanh Commune, Hoi An City, Quang Nam Province, approximately 3–5 kilometers southeast of Hoi An Ancient Town. Its convenient location makes it easy to combine a visit to the historic town with an eco-cultural experience in nature.

The name “Bay Mau,” meaning “Seven Acres,” originates from the forest’s original size of around 70,000 square meters. Over time, thanks to alluvial deposits, the forest has expanded significantly and is now one of the largest and most beautiful water coconut forests in Central Vietnam.

Popular Transportation Options

Visitors can reach Bay Mau Coconut Forest from Hoi An by several means, each offering a different experience:

  • Motorbike: A popular and budget-friendly option, especially among younger travelers. The journey takes about 10–15 minutes and passes scenic rice fields and peaceful villages.

  • Bicycle: Ideal for those who enjoy slow travel and fresh air. The flat and safe route allows you to fully appreciate the rural landscape.

  • Taxi or Grab: Convenient and comfortable for families or groups, with fares ranging from approximately 70,000 to 100,000 VND depending on distance.

  • Tour Bus or Package Tour: Many travel agencies offer half-day or full-day tours that include transportation, entrance fees, and guided activities, allowing for a stress-free experience.

No matter which option you choose, the journey itself is part of the charm, offering a peaceful introduction to the countryside of Hoi An.

Updated Entrance Fees And Basket Boat Ticket Prices 2026

Understanding ticket prices in advance helps you plan your budget more effectively. Below is the latest information on entrance fees and basket boat rental prices for 2026:

Entrance Fee

  • 30,000 VND per person

  • This fee covers entry to the tourist area only and does not include basket boat rides or additional activities.

Basket Boat Ride Price

  • 150,000 VND per basket boat

  • Each basket boat typically accommodates up to two adults

  • The price includes a local boat operator and life jackets

  • Ride duration is approximately 45–60 minutes

Additional Services And Tour Packages

  • Group tours often include entrance tickets, basket boat rides, local meals, and cultural activities at a more competitive price.

  • Larger basket boats for groups of four are available for around 300,000 VND per boat.

  • Prices may vary slightly during peak seasons, holidays, or depending on service providers. Always confirm prices before using services.

Unmissable Experiences At Bay Mau Coconut Forest

Bay Mau Coconut Forest offers much more than scenic views. It is a place where visitors can actively engage in local culture and river-based traditions.

1. Basket Boat Ride Through The Coconut Forest

Glide through winding canals beneath dense coconut palm canopies while local boatmen skillfully navigate the waterways. The cool air, gentle water sounds, and vibrant greenery create a relaxing and immersive experience. You may also spot fish, crabs, and other aquatic life beneath the palms.

2. Watch Traditional Basket Boat Spinning Performances

One of the most exciting highlights is the basket boat spinning show. Local performers demonstrate impressive techniques, spinning and balancing the boats with remarkable skill, creating splashes and cheers from the crowd.

3. Learn Traditional Fishing Techniques

Visitors can try casting fishing nets or catching crabs by hand under the guidance of experienced fishermen. These hands-on activities offer insight into the daily livelihoods of the local community.

4. Make Handicrafts From Coconut Leaves

Participate in a creative workshop where you can learn to make souvenirs such as rings, hats, toys, or small animals from fresh coconut leaves a meaningful keepsake from your visit.

5. Enjoy Local Cuisine

After exploring, enjoy regional specialties such as grilled seafood, banh xeo (Vietnamese savory pancakes), nem lui (lemongrass skewers), and fresh coconut-based desserts at riverside restaurants.

6. Capture Stunning Photos

With its emerald-green scenery, colorful basket boats, and golden sunlight, Bay Mau Coconut Forest is a paradise for photography lovers. Early morning and late afternoon offer the best lighting.

Best Time To Visit Bay Mau Coconut Forest

  • Dry Season (February to August): Ideal weather with minimal rain and clear skies. March to May offers particularly pleasant temperatures.

  • Flood Season (September to November): The forest becomes lush and vibrant, and higher water levels allow deeper exploration, though weather conditions should be monitored.

  • Best Time Of Day: Early morning or late afternoon to avoid strong sunlight and enjoy cooler temperatures.

What To Prepare Before Visiting

  • Sunscreen, hat, sunglasses

  • Light, breathable clothing

  • Comfortable footwear or sandals

  • Camera or smartphone (waterproof bag recommended)

  • Cash for small expenses

  • Personal medications if needed

  • Drinking water and light snacks

Cultural And Historical Significance

Beyond its natural beauty, Bay Mau Coconut Forest holds deep historical value. During the Vietnam War, it served as an important revolutionary base thanks to its dense vegetation and complex waterways. Today, it stands as a symbol of resilience and harmony between people and nature.

Friendly local boat operators are often happy to share stories about the forest’s history and traditions, enriching your visit with meaningful cultural insights.

Important Notes For Visitors

  • Protect the environment and avoid littering

  • Always wear a life jacket during boat rides

  • Politely negotiate prices when traveling independently

  • Respect local customs and traditions

  • Book services in advance during peak seasons

  • Use waterproof bags to protect valuables

Conclusion

Bay Mau Coconut Forest is more than just a tourist attraction it is a unique eco-cultural experience where visitors can reconnect with nature and discover the charm of river life in Central Vietnam. With updated information on basket boat ticket prices for 2026 and practical travel tips, we hope this guide helps you plan a smooth and unforgettable journey to this remarkable destination.

posts.title: Bay Mau Coconut Forest, Hoi An – A Complete Travel Review
posts.excerpt: Bay Mau Coconut Forest, located just a few kilometers from Hoi An Ancient Town, is one of the most distinctive eco-tourism destinations in Central Vietnam. Famous for its lush water coconut palms, pea
posts.contentHtml:
Bay Mau Coconut Forest, located just a few kilometers from Hoi An Ancient Town, is one of the most distinctive eco-tourism destinations in Central Vietnam. Famous for its lush water coconut palms, peaceful waterways, and vibrant local culture, this area offers visitors a chance to experience the authentic river-life lifestyle of rural Vietnam.

From riding traditional basket boats and watching exciting boat-spinning performances to learning coconut-leaf handicrafts and enjoying local cuisine, Bay Mau Coconut Forest promises memorable experiences for travelers visiting Hoi An in 2026.

Where Is Bay Mau Coconut Forest And Its Historical Background

Bay Mau Coconut Forest is located in Cam Thanh Commune, Hoi An City, Quang Nam Province, approximately 3 kilometers from Hoi An Ancient Town. Thanks to its convenient location, visitors can easily reach the forest by motorbike, bicycle, or taxi in about 7–10 minutes.

The name “Bay Mau” (meaning “Seven Acres”) originates from the forest’s original size of around seven acres. Over time, sediment accumulation expanded the forest into a large mangrove ecosystem rich in biodiversity.

Beyond its natural beauty, Bay Mau Coconut Forest also holds historical significance. During the Vietnam War, this dense coconut forest served as a revolutionary base, providing shelter and transportation routes for local resistance forces. Today, stories shared by local boatmen help visitors understand the forest’s important role in history, adding depth to the travel experience.

Best Time To Visit Bay Mau Coconut Forest

Bay Mau Coconut Forest is open year-round, but certain periods offer more favorable conditions:

February To April

This is the best time to visit, with mild temperatures, minimal rain, and comfortable weather for outdoor activities such as basket boat rides, cycling, and photography.

May To July

Although summer can be hot, this period coincides with lively festivals in Hoi An. Travelers often combine a forest visit with beach trips to An Bang or Cua Dai for relaxation.

September To October (Lunar August)

Considered by locals as the most beautiful season, higher water levels allow basket boats to travel deeper into small canals. Light rain enhances the scenery, creating a peaceful and romantic atmosphere.

October To December

This is the rainy and stormy season. While the scenery can be dramatic, travel conditions may be less convenient.

Unmissable Experiences At Bay Mau Coconut Forest

1. Basket Boat Ride Through Coconut Waterways

The highlight of any visit is riding a traditional round basket boat, guided by friendly and experienced local boatmen. Gliding through narrow canals under dense coconut palms offers a refreshing and relaxing escape from busy city life.

2. Basket Boat Spinning Shows And Races

Visitors can enjoy thrilling basket boat spinning performances, showcasing impressive balance and rowing skills. Guests may also participate in fun boat races, creating laughter and unforgettable memories.

3. Coconut Leaf Handicraft Workshop

Learn how to make simple souvenirs such as rings, grasshoppers, fans, or bracelets from fresh coconut leaves. This hands-on activity offers insight into local craftsmanship and daily life.

4. Enjoy Local Cuisine

After exploring the forest, travelers can dine at riverside restaurants serving fresh seafood and regional specialties. Popular dishes include grilled fish, shrimp, Vietnamese pancakes, and coconut-based desserts, accompanied by refreshing fresh coconut water.

5. Cycling Through Cam Thanh Village

Cycling around Cam Thanh village allows visitors to observe rural life, rice fields, traditional houses, and friendly locals. It is an excellent way to experience the peaceful countryside surrounding Hoi An.

6. Fishing With Local Fishermen

For a deeper cultural experience, travelers can join local fishermen to learn traditional fishing techniques such as net casting and crab trapping, followed by enjoying freshly prepared seafood.

7. Visit Nearby Traditional Craft Villages

Nearby villages such as Thanh Ha Pottery Village and Kim Bong Carpentry Village provide additional cultural exploration, where visitors can witness traditional craftsmanship passed down through generations.

Practical Travel Tips

  • Entrance Fee: Approximately 30,000 VND per person

  • Basket Boat Rental: Around 150,000–200,000 VND per boat (2–4 people)

  • What To Wear: Light, comfortable clothing; hat, sunscreen, and sunglasses

  • Safety: Always wear a life jacket during boat rides

  • Environmental Awareness: Help protect the ecosystem by avoiding littering

Accommodation And Nearby Attractions

Visitors can choose from homestays in Cam Thanh for an authentic local experience or hotels and resorts in Hoi An Ancient Town for greater comfort. Bay Mau Coconut Forest is easily combined with visits to Hoi An Old Town, An Bang Beach, Cua Dai Beach, and other cultural landmarks.

Culture And Local Life

What makes Bay Mau Coconut Forest truly special is not only its landscape but also its people. The residents of Cam Thanh are known for their warmth and hospitality. Their knowledge of the forest, traditional basket boats, and sustainable living practices reflect a deep connection with nature.

A visit here offers a refreshing pause from urban life, allowing travelers to reconnect with nature, history, and local traditions in a meaningful way.

Final Thoughts

Bay Mau Coconut Forest is more than just a tourist attraction it is a symbol of resilience, cultural heritage, and sustainable eco-tourism in Hoi An. Whether you are seeking relaxation, cultural discovery, or hands-on experiences, this destination offers something unique and memorable for every traveler.

posts.title: What To Visit When Traveling Independently In Hoi An?
posts.excerpt: Autumn 2026 is an ideal season to explore the ancient and romantic charm of Hoi An. With mild weather, gentle sunshine, and fewer crowds, travelers can leisurely wander lantern-lit streets, visit hist
posts.contentHtml:
Autumn 2026 is an ideal season to explore the ancient and romantic charm of Hoi An. With mild weather, gentle sunshine, and fewer crowds, travelers can leisurely wander lantern-lit streets, visit historic landmarks, and enjoy the city’s rich culinary heritage.

Recognized as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site, Hoi An captivates visitors with its well-preserved ancient town, glowing lanterns, traditional craft villages, and distinctive cuisine. Unlike the vibrant energy of summer or the quiet calm of winter, autumn brings a soft, poetic beauty that allows travelers to experience Hoi An at a slower, more meaningful pace.

Autumn in Hoi An typically lasts from September to November, with average temperatures ranging from 25–30°C. The pleasant climate is perfect for outdoor exploration. On full-moon nights, electric lights are turned off throughout the Old Town and replaced by thousands of lanterns, creating a magical and dreamlike atmosphere that leaves a lasting impression on every visitor.

Must Visit Attractions And Experiences In Hoi An During Autumn 2026

1. Hoi An Lantern Streets – A Magical Nighttime Experience

Lanterns are the soul of Hoi An. As night falls, colorful lanterns illuminate streets, alleys, and ancient houses, creating a romantic and unforgettable scene. Autumn’s cool air enhances the charm, making evening walks especially enjoyable.

Visitors can take a small wooden boat along the Hoai River, release floating lanterns, and admire the glowing Old Town from the water. Lantern-making workshops are also popular, allowing travelers to create their own handmade souvenir inspired by local culture.

2. Ba Mu Temple Gate (Tam Quan Ba Mu) – Ancient Architecture In The Heart Of The Old Town

The Tam Quan Ba Mu Gate is a striking historical structure known for its elegant design and peaceful surroundings. Restored with care, it features a tranquil pond, green lawns, and impressive architectural details that reflect Hoi An’s cultural depth. Autumn brings a calm and serene atmosphere, ideal for photography and quiet reflection.

3. Japanese Covered Bridge – A Cultural Icon Of Hoi An

Also known as Chua Cau, this iconic bridge symbolizes the cultural exchange between Vietnam and Japan during Hoi An’s trading-port era. Its curved roof, intricate carvings, and spiritual significance make it one of the most photographed landmarks in the city. Soft autumn sunlight highlights its timeless beauty.

4. Abandoned Brick Kiln – A Unique Photo Spot

Located about 5 kilometers from the Old Town, an abandoned brick kiln surrounded by rice fields has become a favorite destination for photography enthusiasts. Its raw, rustic appearance contrasts beautifully with the blue autumn sky, offering dramatic and artistic photo opportunities. Sunrise and sunset are the best times to visit.

5. Hoai River – Poetic And Peaceful

Flowing gently through the Old Town, the Hoai River adds a poetic touch to Hoi An’s scenery. In the evening, lantern reflections shimmer on the water as boats glide quietly along. Riverside cafés provide perfect spots to relax, enjoy Vietnamese coffee, and watch life unfold at a slow pace.

6. Thanh Ha Pottery Village – Preserving Traditional Craftsmanship

Situated along the Thu Bon River, Thanh Ha Pottery Village offers insight into centuries-old ceramic traditions. Visitors can watch skilled artisans at work or try shaping pottery themselves. The village’s rustic charm and cultural authenticity make it a meaningful stop for travelers interested in local heritage.

7. Bay Mau Coconut Forest – A “Mini Mekong” Experience

This lush water coconut forest offers a completely different perspective of Hoi An. Guests ride basket boats through narrow waterways, watch traditional fishing demonstrations, and enjoy lively local performances. Autumn’s cooler temperatures make this eco-experience especially comfortable.

8. An Bang And Cua Dai Beaches – Tranquility By The Sea

For those seeking relaxation, An Bang and Cua Dai beaches offer quiet escapes from the Old Town. In autumn, the beaches are peaceful, ideal for seaside walks, watching sunrise or sunset, and enjoying fresh seafood in beachfront restaurants.

9. Fujian Assembly Hall – Chinese Architectural Heritage

This grand assembly hall showcases traditional Chinese architecture with ornate gates, courtyards, and altars dedicated to sea deities. It reflects the historical presence of the Chinese community in Hoi An and is an excellent place to learn about the city’s multicultural past.

10. Tan Ky Ancient House – Living History

Over 200 years old, Tan Ky Ancient House beautifully blends Vietnamese, Japanese, and Chinese architectural elements. Visiting this well-preserved home offers insight into the lifestyle and trading history of Hoi An’s merchant families.

11. Traditional Craft Workshops – Art And Heritage

Hoi An is home to numerous craft workshops producing lanterns, silk, leather goods, and woodwork. Visitors can observe artisans at work, purchase handmade souvenirs, or join short workshops to create personalized keepsakes.

12. Cu Lao Cham Islands – A Natural Paradise

About 15 kilometers offshore, the Cu Lao Cham Islands feature pristine beaches, coral reefs, and traditional fishing villages. Autumn seas are calm, making it a great time for snorkeling, swimming, and enjoying fresh seafood. The islands are recognized as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

13. Hoi An Night Market – Local Flavors And Shopping

As night falls, the night market along the Hoai River becomes lively with lantern stalls, street food vendors, and souvenir shops. It is the perfect place to sample local snacks, shop for handmade items, and experience the vibrant nightlife of Hoi An.

Hoi An Autumn Cuisine – Flavors You Should Not Miss

No trip to Hoi An is complete without tasting its iconic dishes, including:

  • Cao Lau – Thick noodles with roasted pork and fresh herbs

  • Mi Quang – Turmeric noodles with rich but light broth

  • Hoi An Chicken Rice – Fragrant rice with shredded chicken

  • Banh Mi Phuong – Famous Vietnamese baguette

  • White Rose Dumplings – Delicate shrimp-filled dumplings

  • Herbal “Mot” Drink – Refreshing traditional beverage

Travel Tips For Visiting Hoi An In Autumn 2026

  • Book accommodation early, as autumn is a popular travel season

  • Explore the Old Town on foot or by bicycle

  • Bring light layers for cooler evenings

  • Carry some cash for local markets

  • Respect local culture and protect the environment

Final Thoughts

Hoi An in autumn 2026 offers a perfect blend of history, culture, cuisine, and tranquil beauty. From lantern-lit streets and ancient architecture to peaceful rivers and traditional villages, every moment feels poetic and unforgettable. Whether you are a culture lover, a food enthusiast, or a photography fan, Hoi An promises a deeply rewarding journey.

posts.title: Cao Lau Hoi An – The Culinary Essence Of The Ancient Town
posts.excerpt: Cao Lau Hoi An is an iconic dish of the ancient town, embodying the culinary fusion of Vietnamese, Japanese, and Chinese influences. With its distinctive chewy noodles, flavorful char siu pork, and fr
posts.contentHtml:
Cao Lau Hoi An is an iconic dish of the ancient town, embodying the culinary fusion of Vietnamese, Japanese, and Chinese influences. With its distinctive chewy noodles, flavorful char siu pork, and fresh local herbs, each bowl of Cao Lau offers a deep cultural experience telling the story of a once-bustling trading port and the enduring love for food of Hoi An’s people.

Hoi An, an ancient town nestled along the Hoai River, is famous not only for its glowing lantern-lit streets and unique architectural blend but also as a true culinary paradise. Among countless local delicacies, Cao Lau holds a special place, standing as an indispensable symbol of Hoi An’s culinary culture. More than just a dish, Cao Lau is a story of history, cultural exchange, and the passion for food passed down through generations.

1. The Origin and Journey of Cao Lau

Cao Lau appeared in Hoi An hundreds of years ago, during the period when the town was a prosperous trading port with lively exchanges between Vietnam, Japan, China, and Western countries. This dish is a vivid testament to cultural interaction bearing similarities to Chinese cuisine and Japanese noodle-making techniques, yet preserving a unique Vietnamese identity.

The name “Cao Lau” itself sounds elegant and traditional. It is believed to originate from the old term referring to the “upper floors” of ancient eateries, where merchants once sat to enjoy their meals, discuss business, and overlook the bustling streets below.

Thanks to its strategic location on the Maritime Silk Road during the 17th–18th centuries, Hoi An became a cultural crossroads. This convergence gave rise to a diverse culinary heritage, with Cao Lau as one of its finest representatives. While its noodles may resemble Japanese udon or Chinese noodles, the preparation and flavor are entirely distinctive showcasing the creativity and refinement of local people.

Cao Lau is not a coincidence but the result of thoughtful adaptation to local tastes and ingredients. It is not merely food, but a living part of Hoi An’s history, carrying centuries of prosperity and cultural exchange.

2. The Unique and Elaborate Preparation of Cao Lau

What makes Cao Lau truly special lies in its meticulous and elaborate preparation, from ingredient selection to execution skills passed down through generations. Each step is an art form in itself.

Cao Lau Noodles – The Soul of the Dish

The noodles are the most important element, defining the identity of Cao Lau. Unlike pho or vermicelli, Cao Lau noodles are made from local rice soaked in ash water derived from trees on Cham Island. This ash water gives the noodles their light yellow hue and signature chewy, crispy texture.

Even more uniquely, the dough must be kneaded using water from Ba Le Well, an ancient well in Hoi An believed to contain ideal minerals that give the noodles their perfect elasticity and purity of flavor. The dough is then rested, rolled, hand-cut, steamed, and sun-dried to achieve the ideal firmness and sheen.

The “Sacred” Broth

Unlike noodle soups, Cao Lau uses very little broth just enough to coat the noodles. The sauce is simmered from pork bones and char siu drippings, resulting in a thick, amber-colored sauce with a rich yet balanced sweetness. Long simmering and careful seasoning create a glossy, aromatic base that ties all ingredients together.

Char Siu Pork – A Chinese Touch

Pork belly is marinated with five-spice powder, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, and a touch of honey, then slowly braised or grilled until tender inside with a caramelized exterior. Thinly sliced, the pork adds depth, sweetness, and aroma to the dish.

Fresh Herbs – A Taste of the Countryside

Cao Lau is served with a variety of fresh herbs such as mustard greens, basil, fish mint, and bean sprouts. Most notably, these herbs come from Tra Que Vegetable Village, known for organic farming and distinctive flavors. The freshness of the herbs balances the richness of the noodles and pork.

Crispy Noodles and Fried Pork Rind

Crispy fried noodle bits and crunchy pork rind are added for texture and richness. These elements enhance both flavor and mouthfeel, making each bite more exciting.

3. Enjoying Cao Lau – A Cultural Experience

Eating Cao Lau in Hoi An is more than a meal it is a cultural journey. Locals often say Cao Lau is the soul of Hoi An, a flavor of memory that lingers long after leaving.

The dish is commonly served in small street-side eateries or traditional restaurants. Sitting on rustic wooden stools, watching life pass by in the ancient town, savoring each chewy noodle and fragrant slice of pork, diners feel transported back to Hoi An’s golden trading days.

The best time to enjoy Cao Lau is early morning, when the town is quiet, or at dusk, when lanterns begin to glow. Famous spots include Ba Thanh (Tran Cao Van Street), Lien Restaurant (Thai Phien Street), and Trung Bac (Tran Phu Street). Prices range from 30,000–50,000 VND per bowl remarkably affordable for such a unique culinary experience. Pair it with a glass of Mot herbal drink or traditional tea for a complete meal.

4. The Harmony of Ingredients

Every component of Cao Lau plays a vital role none can be omitted. The chewy noodles, savory pork, concentrated sauce, and fresh herbs create a perfectly balanced dish that has become a must-try for visitors to Hoi An.

From the uniquely prepared noodles to the carefully marinated pork, from the lightly coated sauce to the crisp rice crackers and fried noodles, Cao Lau offers layers of texture and flavor that are both refined and comforting.

5. The Flavor Profile – Subtle and Complex

A single bite of Cao Lau reveals a symphony of flavors: chewy noodles, rich pork, fresh herbs, gentle sweetness, and subtle richness. The dish is savory yet light, flavorful without being heavy.

Its presentation is simple yet elegant golden noodles at the base, thin slices of pork on top, vibrant greens, crispy rice crackers, and a drizzle of thick sauce. Diners mix everything together to fully experience the harmony. A bit of Hoi An chili sauce or lime juice can be added to taste.

Cao Lau is not just food it is a multi-sensory experience that reflects the care, craftsmanship, and cultural pride of Hoi An’s people.

6. Cao Lau in the Lives of Locals and Visitors

For locals, Cao Lau is a daily staple and a source of pride. Many families preserve their own secret recipes, passing them down through generations. Long-standing eateries have become gathering places for both locals and travelers, offering warmth and authenticity.

Cao Lau is typically enjoyed for breakfast or lunch, but also as an afternoon treat. Prices remain affordable, from 25,000–40,000 VND, making it accessible to all visitors. To find the most authentic flavor, ask locals or seek out small, unassuming eateries sometimes the best bowls come from the simplest places.

Cao Lau also appears at festivals and cultural events, symbolizing the fusion of cultures and the enduring spirit of Hoi An. Discovering Cao Lau means discovering the soul of the ancient town itself.

Cao Lau Hoi An is a dish defined not only by its taste but by the story it tells. Its careful preparation, local ingredients, and deep cultural roots make it both humble and refined a true culinary treasure of the ancient town.

To taste Cao Lau is to step into the rhythm of Hoi An life, to connect past and present, and to fall in love with a land rich in tradition. When visiting Hoi An, be sure to seek out local eateries and let a bowl of Cao Lau tell you the timeless story of this enchanting town.

posts.title: Travel Tips For Visiting Hoi An In Autumn – Discover A Truly Unique Beauty
posts.excerpt: Hoi An in the autumn of 2026 reveals a romantic and contemplative charm, with cool, pleasant weather and gentle drizzles. Visitors can explore the ancient town by bicycle, enjoy traditional cuisine, j
posts.contentHtml:
Hoi An in the autumn of 2026 reveals a romantic and contemplative charm, with cool, pleasant weather and gentle drizzles. Visitors can explore the ancient town by bicycle, enjoy traditional cuisine, join lantern-making workshops, and learn about local culture at historic landmarks.

Hoi An, a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site, has always been radiant and captivating no matter the season. The town possesses a nostalgic, ancient, and poetic beauty, further enhanced by the warmth and kindness of its local people. However, traveling to Hoi An in autumn offers something truly special an atmosphere of peace and romance that is hard to find elsewhere.

Autumn brings a deeper, more soulful beauty to the ancient town, making every step feel as if you are wandering through a fairytale. Let’s discover the unique charm and unforgettable experiences that await you in Hoi An during the romantic autumn of 2026.

Hoi An in Autumn – A Quiet and Romantic Charm

The Best Time to Explore Hoi An in Autumn

Autumn in Hoi An usually arrives later than in other regions, lasting from September to November. Early in the season, gentle traces of summer sunshine remain, but the weather is no longer harsh. The sunlight becomes softer and more pleasant, creating ideal conditions for sightseeing.

Daytime temperatures range from 25–30°C, with cooler evenings, making it perfect for walking, cycling, or taking a boat ride. This is a wonderful time to stroll through ancient streets, admire unique architecture, and experience the slow-paced lifestyle of local residents.

Autumn mornings in Hoi An are often wrapped in light mist, creating a dreamy and poetic atmosphere. Visitors can rent bicycles or walk around the old town, breathe in the fresh air, and watch the streets slowly come to life. Stop by a small café near the Japanese Covered Bridge, enjoy a rich cup of Vietnamese coffee, and soak in the peaceful beauty of Hoi An. The gentle morning sounds and calm rhythm of daily life bring a rare sense of relaxation and inner peace especially during early autumn when tourist crowds are still minimal.

When night falls, Hoi An transforms into a completely different scene romantic and glowing. Thousands of colorful lanterns illuminate the ancient town with warm light. On the 14th day of the lunar month, electric lights are turned off, allowing lanterns to shine in front of every house. Visitors can also take part in the lantern-floating ceremony on the Hoai River, sending wishes for good fortune. This unique cultural experience is deeply rooted in Hoi An’s traditions.

The Quiet Beauty and Unique Photo Spots of Hoi An in the Rainy Season

By November, Hoi An begins to welcome light drizzles and the cool air of late autumn. While rain may seem inconvenient, it actually enhances the town’s nostalgic and ancient beauty. Moss-covered tiled roofs and weathered walls appear fresher and greener, creating a scene reminiscent of an ink-wash painting.

Raindrops resting on bougainvillea flowers and old rooftops create artistic frames that are impossible to find in other seasons. Many compare Hoi An in autumn rain to a slow-motion film of the past simple, poetic, and untouched by time.

This is an ideal time to explore the cultural and historical depth of the town. Visitors can visit attractions such as the Hoi An Museum of Trade Ceramics, the Japanese Covered Bridge, ancient Chinese assembly halls, or even the nearby My Son Sanctuary. Walking along the peaceful Hoai River, watching boats drift gently by, offers a rare sense of calm. Don’t forget to bring your camera to capture the “one-of-a-kind” moments of Hoi An in the rain.

Autumn Cuisine in Hoi An – Warmth and Nostalgic Flavors

Autumn in Hoi An is not only beautiful but also irresistible when it comes to food, especially dishes suited for cool weather. Try a bowl of hot Cao Lau, featuring chewy noodles, savory char siu pork, and fresh herbs. Enjoy Mi Quang, with its rich broth, fresh shrimp and meat, and crispy rice crackers.

Don’t miss White Rose dumplings, soft steamed buns, or crispy fried wontons. These dishes are more than just local specialties they represent the soul of Hoi An’s culinary heritage.

On rainy days, there’s nothing better than sitting by a warm stove enjoying hot sweet corn pudding or ginger tofu dessert. Street food such as Banh Mi Phuong, ice cream tubes, and traditional sweet soups are also must-try experiences. Food prices are very reasonable, usually ranging from 30,000 to 100,000 VND per dish. For a deeper culinary experience, visitors can join local cooking classes to learn traditional recipes.

How to Enjoy Hoi An in Autumn on Rainy Days

Autumn in Hoi An sometimes brings sudden rain, but that only adds to the town’s charm. Here are some great ways to enjoy your trip even when it drizzles.

Relax at Vintage Cafés and Indoor Spaces

When rain interrupts outdoor plans, head to a vintage café or a cozy bar in the old town. Many cafés overlook the Hoai River and are decorated in nostalgic styles. Sitting by the window with a hot cup of coffee while watching the rain fall over the ancient streets is incredibly poetic.

Some cafés offer rooftop views, fresh fruit drinks, homemade ice cream, and French-style pastries perfect for reading, chatting, or simply relaxing. Visitors can also explore art galleries, handicraft shops, or join workshops such as painting or pottery making.

Traditional Lantern-Making and Handicraft Experiences

Lantern-making is one of Hoi An’s most iconic traditional crafts. Lanterns not only serve as handicrafts but also create the magical nighttime atmosphere of the ancient town.

Rainy days are the perfect opportunity to join a lantern-making workshop, where you’ll learn step by step from selecting bamboo frames to decorating with silk fabric. Creating your own lantern is both a fun experience and a meaningful souvenir that reflects Hoi An’s culture. Visitors can also explore other traditional villages such as Kim Bong Carpentry Village or Tra Que Vegetable Village for deeper cultural insight.

Exploring Historical and Cultural Landmarks

Hoi An is a living museum filled with valuable historical sites. On rainy days, visitors can explore indoor attractions such as the Sa Huynh Culture Museum, Museum of Trade Ceramics, and famous ancient houses like Tan Ky House or Phung Hung House. Each site tells stories of Hoi An’s formation and its once-thriving trading past.

Chinese assembly halls such as Fujian Assembly Hall and Trieu Chau Assembly Hall are also fascinating places to admire architecture and learn about the customs and beliefs of the Chinese community in Hoi An.

Enjoy Traditional Arts and Shop for Local Specialties

Hoi An is also a center of traditional arts. On rainy days, visitors can attend performances such as Bai Choi singing, water puppetry, or traditional dances at small theaters and cultural centers.

Shopping is another enjoyable activity from silk products and handcrafted leather goods to pottery and artwork. Traditional markets like Hoi An Market offer a lively atmosphere and plenty of local snacks to try.

Hoi An in autumn stands out with its nostalgic, poetic, and timeless beauty something few destinations can replicate. From scenery and architecture to gentle weather, romantic rain, rich cuisine, and immersive cultural experiences, everything comes together to create a truly unforgettable journey.

To make your trip smoother, remember to plan transportation and book accommodation in advance, especially if you’re traveling during popular periods.

posts.title: Hoi An Autumn Travel – Discover The Poetic Beauty Of The Ancient Town
posts.excerpt: Autumn in Hoi An in 2026 promises a gentle, romantic charm with pleasant weather and a peaceful atmosphere. Visitors can explore the town’s deep cultural heritage, enjoy refined local cuisine, and tak
posts.contentHtml:
Autumn in Hoi An in 2026 promises a gentle, romantic charm with pleasant weather and a peaceful atmosphere. Visitors can explore the town’s deep cultural heritage, enjoy refined local cuisine, and take part in unique traditional activities far away from the noise and rush of modern life.

Hoi An Ancient Town, a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site, captivates visitors with its timeless beauty throughout the year. However, when autumn arrives, Hoi An seems to put on a new cloak softer, quieter, and more romantic than ever. This is the perfect time for travelers to return to ancient values, immerse themselves in picturesque scenery, and feel the warmth and simplicity of the local people.

An autumn trip to Hoi An offers unforgettable experiences, where you can slow down, enjoy the tranquility, and escape the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Let’s explore with Vietlook Travel what makes Hoi An so special in the autumn of 2026.

Experiencing Hoi An in Autumn

Hoi An in Autumn – A Harmonious Blend of Nature and Culture

Autumn in Hoi An usually lasts from September to November. In the early months, particularly September and October, traces of summer sunshine remain, but the heat is no longer harsh. Instead, golden sunlight gently bathes the ancient streets, creating a warm and comforting atmosphere. The average temperature ranges from 25–30°C, making it ideal for outdoor exploration.

Light autumn breezes carry the scent of newly harvested rice and a subtle chill, adding to the town’s romantic and relaxing ambiance. Visiting Hoi An during this time allows travelers to fully appreciate the beauty of the ancient town without the crowds typical of peak tourist season.

In the early morning, when mist still lingers, renting a bicycle and leisurely riding through narrow alleys lined with moss-covered roofs and vibrant bougainvillea is a delightful experience. Stop by a riverside café along the Hoai River, sip a cup of rich Vietnamese coffee, and listen to the gentle rustling of falling leaves you’ll feel a deep sense of peace. Autumn is also the perfect season for photography, capturing Hoi An’s simple yet captivating moments.

On the 14th day of the lunar month, Hoi An becomes especially enchanting during the Lantern Festival. Electric lights are turned off, replaced by the warm glow of thousands of colorful lanterns hanging in front of houses and floating lanterns drifting along the Hoai River. Releasing a lantern while making a wish is a deeply meaningful cultural experience that leaves visitors in awe.

Hoi An in the Drizzle – A Different Kind of Beauty

By November, Hoi An enters late autumn and early winter, with gentle drizzles and cooler air. While some travelers hesitate to visit during the rainy season, Hoi An in the rain reveals a unique charm more nostalgic and serene than ever.

Rain washes over mossy rooftops and ancient walls, bringing out deeper shades of green and enhancing the town’s poetic beauty. On rainy days, instead of strolling outdoors, visitors can relax in vintage cafés, enjoy a hot cup of tea or coffee, and watch life slowly pass by.

This is also the perfect time to enjoy warm local dishes such as Cao Lau, Mi Quang, and wontons, or to explore museums and historic houses like Tan Ky Ancient House and Fujian Assembly Hall, where architectural and historical values are beautifully preserved.

Beyond the ancient town, autumn is ideal for visiting traditional craft villages. Tra Que Vegetable Village appears especially picturesque under light rain, while Kim Bong Carpentry Village offers insight into the craftsmanship of local artisans. These excursions provide a deeper cultural connection and a refreshing escape from urban life.

Why Choose Hoi An for an Autumn Getaway?

Traveling to Hoi An in autumn offers many unexpected advantages:

  • Pleasant weather and poetic scenery: Mild temperatures and soft sunlight make it ideal for walking, cycling, and sightseeing. Beaches like An Bang and Cua Dai remain beautiful and tranquil, perfect for relaxing strolls.

  • Fewer crowds, more authentic experiences: Autumn is not peak season, allowing visitors to explore at a slower pace and interact more closely with locals.

  • Unique cultural festivals: In addition to the Lantern Festival, autumn may coincide with the Mid-Autumn Festival, filling the town with colorful lanterns and lively performances.

  • Cost savings: Airfares, hotels, and tour services are generally more affordable compared to peak season.

  • Seasonal culinary delights: Cooler weather enhances the enjoyment of Hoi An’s famous dishes and local desserts.

Must Do Activities in Hoi An During Autumn

  • Boat ride on the Hoai River: Enjoy lantern-lit views at sunset or evening. Prices range from 100,000–200,000 VND for a 20–30 minute ride.

  • Join a cooking class: Learn to prepare local specialties and discover the secrets of Hoi An cuisine.

  • Explore historical landmarks: Visit the Japanese Covered Bridge, Chinese Assembly Halls, and ancient houses. Entrance tickets to the old town range from 80,000–120,000 VND, depending on nationality.

  • Relax at nearby beaches: An Bang and Cua Dai beaches are calm and beautiful in autumn.

  • Shop for souvenirs: Lanterns, silk products, handicrafts, and leather goods are popular choices.

Travel Tips for a Perfect Autumn Trip

  • Bring light clothing for daytime and a thin jacket for cooler evenings or rainy days.

  • Walking and cycling are the best ways to explore the ancient town.

  • Book accommodation in advance for better options and prices.

  • Try street food such as white rose dumplings, banh bao, and sweet corn pudding.

  • Respect local customs, especially when visiting temples and historical sites.

Autumn in Hoi An – History Whispering Through Old Streets

Autumn is also the perfect season to explore the historical depth of Hoi An. Each street and ancient house tells stories of a once-thriving trading port in the 17th–18th centuries, where Vietnamese, Japanese, Chinese, and Western merchants gathered.

Don’t miss the Japanese Covered Bridge, the symbol of Hoi An, built in the 17th century. Under soft autumn sunlight, its curved roof and ancient structure create a magical scene. Assembly halls such as Fujian and Cantonese Halls also offer insight into the spiritual life of the Chinese community.

For history lovers, museums like the Sa Huynh Culture Museum and the Museum of Trade Ceramics provide valuable archaeological and cultural perspectives, best enjoyed in the calm atmosphere of autumn.

Autumn Cuisine in Hoi An – Delicate and Memorable Flavors

Cooler weather makes Hoi An’s cuisine even more irresistible:

  • Cao Lau: Chewy noodles, char siu pork, fresh herbs, and rich sauce (30,000–50,000 VND).

  • Mi Quang: A signature Central Vietnamese noodle dish with savory broth (25,000–40,000 VND).

  • Banh Mi Phuong: World-famous Vietnamese baguette (20,000–30,000 VND).

  • Wontons: Fried or in broth, adapted to local taste.

  • Cam Nam sweet corn dessert: Light, creamy, and refreshing.

Traditional Craft Villages and Cultural Activities

  • Tra Que Vegetable Village: Experience organic farming and enjoy farm-to-table meals.

  • Kim Bong Carpentry Village: Discover traditional woodcraft.

  • Thanh Ha Pottery Village: Try making pottery by hand.

  • Lantern-making workshops: Create your own Hoi An lantern (100,000–150,000 VND).

Final Tips for Hoi An Autumn Travel 2026

  • Choose accommodation based on your budget from homestays to luxury resorts.

  • Rent bicycles (20,000–30,000 VND/day) or enjoy a cyclo ride.

  • Autumn lighting is perfect for photography dress in vintage or neutral tones.

  • Shop for handmade lanterns, silk, leather goods, and souvenirs.

  • Bring sunscreen, water, and personal medication despite the mild weather.

Hoi An in autumn is more than a destination it is a journey back to timeless values, where life slows down and beauty reveals itself quietly.

We hope this guide helps you plan a meaningful and unforgettable autumn trip to Hoi An in 2026.

posts.contentHtml:
Bay Mau Coconut Forest, a popular attraction near Hoi An, is famous for its unique bamboo basket boat experience. This article provides useful tips on renting basket boats at affordable prices, the ideal time to visit, local specialties, and practical notes for your trip in 2026.

Bay Mau Coconut Forest has become an increasingly popular tourist destination, attracting a large number of visitors. Traveling to Bay Mau Coconut Forest in Hoi An in the summer of 2026 promises unforgettable experiences, especially the chance to explore the area by traditional basket boat. So how can you rent a basket boat at a reasonable price? Let’s explore the answer together with Vietlook Travel in the article below.

Da Nang Travel: Affordable Basket Boat Rental at Bay Mau Coconut Forest

Where Is Bay Mau Coconut Forest Located?

Bay Mau Coconut Forest is a well-known tourist attraction located in Cam Thanh Commune, Hoi An City, Quang Nam Province. It lies only about 3 km southeast of Hoi An Ancient Town, making it very convenient for visitors to travel and explore. Thanks to this prime location, Bay Mau Coconut Forest is an ideal destination to combine with a Hoi An sightseeing itinerary.

This vast water coconut forest is situated at the confluence of the Co Co River and Thu Bon River, forming a unique mangrove ecosystem. Since ancient times, it has provided abundant aquatic resources and acted as a natural shield protecting local residents from floods and storms. Today, Bay Mau Coconut Forest not only plays an important environmental role but also attracts visitors with its untouched beauty and distinctive Central Vietnamese river culture.

The Origin of the Name “Bay Mau Coconut Forest”

The name “Bay Mau Coconut Forest” originates from the forest’s original size. In the 18th century, the forest covered only about seven mẫu (approximately 70,000 square meters). However, thanks to favorable natural conditions such as brackish water and a tropical monsoon climate, water coconut trees thrived and gradually expanded to an area of over 100 hectares.

Despite its significant expansion, the name “Bay Mau” has been preserved by locals and visitors as a way to honor the forest’s history and long-standing connection with the land. More than just a number, the name carries cultural value and reflects the early days when the coconut forest was first formed and became a symbol of the Cam Thanh river region.

What’s Attractive About a Bay Mau Coconut Forest Tour?

Bay Mau Coconut Forest resembles a miniature version of the Mekong Delta right in the heart of Central Vietnam. Visitors are immersed in a refreshing green space of endless water coconut trees stretching along small canals. The highlight experience here is riding a basket boat, a traditional means of transportation used by local fishermen.

Sitting on a basket boat, you’ll be skillfully guided through narrow waterways, enjoying the peaceful atmosphere while discovering the area’s rich ecosystem.

In addition, visitors can watch impressive basket boat spinning performances by local artisans. The skillful spinning and balancing techniques on the small round boats are sure to amaze you. You may also try rowing a basket boat yourself under the guidance of locals an unforgettable hands-on experience.

Other activities include learning how to make handicrafts from coconut leaves (rings, hats, watches), participating in folk games on the water such as basket boat racing, tug-of-war, or fishing. These activities offer a wonderful chance to connect with local life and explore the unique river culture of Hoi An.

Best Time to Visit Bay Mau Coconut Forest

The ideal time to visit Bay Mau Coconut Forest is during the dry season, from February to September. During this period, the weather in Hoi An is usually sunny, dry, and pleasant—perfect for outdoor activities like basket boat rides and sightseeing.

The best months are March to May, when temperatures are mild and comfortable. If you enjoy lively atmospheres and traditional festivals, consider visiting during major holidays or on full-moon days (lunar calendar) to combine your trip with a nighttime visit to Hoi An Ancient Town.

If you prefer a quieter experience, it’s best to visit on weekdays and avoid peak midday hours.

Local Cuisine at Bay Mau Coconut Forest

Visiting Bay Mau Coconut Forest is not only about nature but also about food. Restaurants and small eateries around the area serve a variety of fresh seafood, including fish, shrimp, crabs, and snails caught locally.

You shouldn’t miss dishes made from water coconut, such as coconut salad, coconut sweet soup, and fresh coconut drinks. After the forest tour, you can also enjoy famous Hoi An specialties like Mi Quang, Cao Lau, banh vac (white rose dumplings), and wontons.

How to Get to Bay Mau Coconut Forest

There are several ways to travel from Hoi An city center to Bay Mau Coconut Forest:

  • Motorbike: The most popular and flexible option, allowing you to enjoy scenic views along the way. Travel time is about 10–15 minutes.

  • Bicycle: Ideal for those who enjoy a peaceful pace and fresh air. The route is short and flat.

  • Taxi or Grab: A comfortable option for families or groups with children.

  • Boat: Some tours offer boat transfers from Hoi An Ancient Town to the coconut forest, providing a unique experience from the start.

Basket Boat Rental Prices at Bay Mau Coconut Forest

Basket boat rides are a must-do activity at Bay Mau Coconut Forest. Current prices (updated 2025) are as follows:

  • Entrance ticket: 30,000 VND per person

  • Basket boat ride: Approximately 200,000 – 250,000 VND per boat (maximum 2 adults and 1 child)

Prices may vary slightly depending on the season and your bargaining skills.

On average, the total cost per person ranges from 130,000 – 155,000 VND if two people share a boat—quite reasonable for such a unique experience.

Tips for Renting Basket Boats Cheaply and Effectively

  • Travel in groups: Sharing a basket boat helps reduce costs significantly.

  • Book online in advance: Many travel agencies offer combo packages at better prices. Booking at least one day ahead is recommended.

  • Avoid buying tickets directly at the entrance: Prices are often higher and harder to negotiate.

  • Choose off-peak times: Visit on weekdays or early morning/late afternoon for fewer crowds and better deals.

  • Ask about included services: Some tours include performances, handicraft activities, or local food—make sure you get full value.

Other Important Notes When Visiting Bay Mau Coconut Forest

  • Clothing: Wear comfortable, breathable clothes and easy-to-walk footwear. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen.

  • Environmental protection: Keep the area clean and avoid damaging plants or littering.

  • Bring a camera: The lush green scenery is perfect for photos—don’t miss it.

  • Interact with locals: Local people are friendly and welcoming. Talking with them will enrich your experience.

In conclusion, Vietlook Travel has shared detailed information about Bay Mau Coconut Forest, including affordable basket boat rental tips and essential travel notes. We hope these insights will help make your upcoming Da Nang – Hoi An tour more memorable and enjoyable, offering truly unique and meaningful experiences.

posts.title: Summary Of 3 Important Notes When Joining Da Nang Tour
posts.excerpt: Da Nang in 2026 promises an exciting journey of discovery with stunning beaches, diverse cuisine, and a unique cultural identity. This article provides a detailed travel guide from the ideal time to v
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang in 2026 promises an exciting journey of discovery with stunning beaches, diverse cuisine, and a unique cultural identity. This article provides a detailed travel guide from the ideal time to visit and accommodation choices to smart transportation and shopping tips to help you enjoy a perfect and memorable trip. Don’t miss the suggested 3 day 2 night itinerary to fully experience the beauty of this charming coastal city.

Da Nang, a young and dynamic city and one of Vietnam’s top travel destinations, continues to attract a large number of visitors. With continuously developing infrastructure and tourism services, Da Nang has firmly established itself as a “most livable city,” boasting beautiful beaches, rich cuisine, and friendly locals. If you are planning to explore this coastal city in 2026 whether on a package tour or traveling independently understanding the important notes below will help make your trip smoother and more enjoyable.

3 Important Notes for Travelers Joining a Da Nang Combo Tour

1. Best Time to Visit Da Nang

Da Nang has a tropical monsoon climate with two distinct seasons:

  • Dry season: January to July

  • Rainy season: August to December

Choosing the right time to travel greatly affects your experience.

According to many travelers, May to July is the best time to visit Da Nang. During this period, the weather is dry and sunny with little rain—ideal for sightseeing, outdoor activities, and especially swimming at famous beaches like My Khe and Non Nuoc. The average temperature ranges from 28–32°C. This is also the peak tourist season, so service prices may be slightly higher.

Another great option is January to April, when the weather is cooler and more pleasant, with less intense sunshine and minimal rain. Traveling during this period can help you save costs, as airfare and hotel prices are usually lower than in peak season. It’s perfect for those who want a more relaxed experience and fewer crowds.

The rainy season (August–December) may bring sudden showers or storms, but it’s suitable for travelers who enjoy peace and a quieter atmosphere. Indoor activities such as visiting museums, enjoying local cuisine, or relaxing at spas are great alternatives.

You can also plan your trip around festivals to experience local culture, such as the Da Nang International Fireworks Festival (DIFF) held in summer. Photography lovers will enjoy the dry season’s clear skies and golden sunlight, while the rainy season can create a romantic, mystical charm—especially at places like Ban Co Peak or Hai Van Pass.

2. Choosing Suitable Accommodation in Da Nang

As a major tourism hub, Da Nang offers a wide range of accommodations—from luxury resorts and high-end hotels to budget guesthouses and unique homestays.

If convenience and easy transportation are your priorities, choose hotels in the city center or near the airport, where you’ll have easy access to restaurants, shopping malls, and famous bridges like Dragon Bridge and Han River Bridge.
For beach lovers, My Khe or Non Nuoc beachfront hotels are ideal for enjoying fresh sea air and sunrise views.

Budget travelers can opt for guesthouses or homestays in suburban areas or small alleys, which are more affordable. Some homestays offer unique local cultural experiences with cozy, friendly designs.

Tips:

  • Book accommodation 1–3 months in advance, especially during peak seasons or holidays.

  • Booking through travel agencies or online platforms often offers better deals than booking directly.

  • Check amenities such as swimming pools, gyms, spas, and restaurants.

  • Read guest reviews to ensure service quality.

3. Exploring Local Cuisine and Culture

Da Nang’s cuisine is a major highlight. Don’t miss iconic dishes such as Mi Quang, fish cake noodle soup, banh xeo, nem lui, and Nam O fish salad. Each dish reflects the flavors of Central Vietnam, using fresh ingredients and traditional recipes.

For authentic food experiences, visit local markets like Con Market and Han Market, which are also street food paradises with reasonable prices. Don’t hesitate to try local snacks and chat with vendors to learn more about culinary culture.

Culturally, Da Nang blends modern urban life with long-standing traditions. Visit the Cham Museum to learn about ancient Champa civilization, or explore traditional craft villages like Non Nuoc Stone Village. If possible, attend local festivals to gain deeper insight into the city’s spiritual life.

Other must-try specialties include pork rolled with rice paper, fermented fish sauce noodles, and local sweet soups (chè). Street food stalls often offer the most authentic flavors at affordable prices. You can even join local cooking classes to better understand Central Vietnamese cuisine.

Transportation and Smart Shopping Tips

Transportation options in Da Nang include taxis, ride-hailing services (Grab, Gojek), and motorbike rentals (around 100,000–150,000 VND/day). Public buses are also available for budget travelers.

When shopping for souvenirs or local specialties, always ask for prices in advance and check product quality. Popular specialties include dried squid, dried fish, Nam O fish sauce, sesame crackers, and Non Nuoc stone products.

For longer trips to places like Hoi An or Ba Na Hills, consider hiring a car with a driver or using tourist buses for convenience.

Additional Tips When Traveling to Da Nang

  • Bring sun protection when going to the beach (hat, sunscreen, sunglasses).

  • Avoid swimming at night for safety reasons.

  • Bridge schedules:

    • Han River Bridge rotates from 11:00 PM to 12:00 AM on weekends.

    • Dragon Bridge breathes fire and water at 9:00 PM on Saturday and Sunday nights.

  • Keep the environment clean and avoid littering.

  • Carry some cash for small vendors and markets.

  • Prepare a small first-aid kit and a power bank for your devices.

Suggested 3 Day 2 Night Da Nang Itinerary

Day 1: City Center & My Khe Beach

  • Morning: Arrive, check in, enjoy Mi Quang, visit Cham Museum

  • Afternoon: Swim and relax at My Khe Beach

  • Evening: Visit Dragon Bridge & Han River Bridge, enjoy seafood

Day 2: Ba Na Hills & Hoi An

  • Daytime: Explore Ba Na Hills (Golden Bridge, French Village, Fantasy Park)

  • Evening: Visit Hoi An Ancient Town, lantern release, enjoy local dishes

Day 3: Marble Mountains & Shopping

  • Morning: Visit Marble Mountains and Non Nuoc Stone Village

  • Afternoon: Shop for souvenirs at Han or Con Market

  • Evening: Head to the airport, end the trip

Above is a complete guide and essential tips to help you enjoy a perfect and memorable Da Nang trip in 2026. We hope this information helps you plan your journey smoothly. Wishing you an amazing trip filled with beautiful memories in Da Nang.

posts.title: The Dreamy Beauty Of Nam O Reef In Da Nang
posts.excerpt: If you have already visited Da Nang, explored its famous attractions in the city center, and are now looking for a peaceful place with poetic natural scenery, Nam O Reef is truly a perfect choice. For
posts.contentHtml:
If you have already visited Da Nang, explored its famous attractions in the city center, and are now looking for a peaceful place with poetic natural scenery, Nam O Reef is truly a perfect choice.

For nature lovers and travelers who enjoy discovering new destinations away from crowds and noise, Nam O Reef offers a refreshing and tranquil escape during your Da Nang journey. Let’s explore with Vietlook Travel what makes Nam O Reef so special and why it attracts so many visitors.

Where Is Nam O Reef Located?

Nam O Reef is located about 17 kilometers from Da Nang city center, in Hiep Hoa Ward, Lien Chieu District, Da Nang. The beach has existed since the 1960s and was originally a local spot for swimming and relaxation. Today, Nam O Reef has become one of the most attractive destinations for travelers who wish to explore the peaceful and untouched beauty of Da Nang’s coastline.

How To Get To Nam O Reef In Da Nang

The road leading to Nam O Reef is wide and easy to access, making it convenient to travel by either motorbike or car. If you enjoy adventurous road trips and scenic views along the way, riding a motorbike is a great option. On the other hand, if you are traveling with family or in a large group and prefer comfort and safety, traveling by car is more suitable.

Suggested route:
From Da Nang city center, go straight along Ton Duc Thang Street, continue to Nguyen Luong Bang Street, pass Xuan Thieu Beach, then turn onto a small road leading to the fishing village. From there, you will reach Nam O Reef.

What Makes Nam O Reef Worth Visiting?

Here are some memorable experiences you should not miss when visiting Nam O Reef during your Da Nang tour:

Take Stunning Photos At The Moss-Covered Rocky Shore

With its dreamy natural scenery, Nam O Reef is a favorite check-in spot for photography lovers. The highlight of this area is the rocky shoreline covered in vibrant green moss, especially beautiful during early morning or sunset. These unique natural formations create breathtaking photo opportunities that will make your travel album truly stand out.

Admire The Untouched Beauty Of Nam O Beach

Unlike the busy and crowded beaches in central Da Nang, Nam O Reef remains largely undeveloped, preserving its rare wild and natural charm. Visitors will be impressed by the clear blue seawater, long stretches of white sand, and the peaceful atmosphere. This untouched beauty makes Nam O Reef an ideal destination for those seeking serenity and a close connection with nature.

Visit The Traditional Nam O Fish Sauce Village

Nam O Fish Sauce is one of the most famous traditional specialties of Da Nang. Made primarily from anchovies caught locally, this fish sauce has been produced using traditional methods for generations. When visiting the Nam O Fish Sauce Village, travelers can learn about the production process and gain deeper insight into the daily lives and cultural heritage of local fishermen.

Camping And Picnicking By The Sea

Nam O Reef is also an excellent location for camping and outdoor picnics. Surrounded by vast natural landscapes and the sound of gentle waves, visitors can enjoy a sense of peace and relaxation far away from the hustle and bustle of city life. This is a perfect way to unwind and recharge after busy workdays.

Conclusion

Nam O Reef has a unique charm that captivates many travelers visiting Da Nang. A trip here not only offers stunning check-in photos but also unforgettable experiences immersed in nature and local culture. If you have fallen in love with Da Nang’s beautiful coastline, be sure not to miss the chance to explore the serene and picturesque Nam O Reef.

posts.title: Nam O Fish Salad – The Culinary Essence Of A Traditional Fishing Village In Da Nang
posts.excerpt: When mentioning Da Nang travel in 2026, many people immediately think of long white-sand beaches, iconic bridges glowing at night, or the majestic Son Tra Peninsula. However, what truly creates the ci
posts.contentHtml:
When mentioning Da Nang travel in 2026, many people immediately think of long white-sand beaches, iconic bridges glowing at night, or the majestic Son Tra Peninsula. However, what truly creates the city’s lasting charm is its rich and distinctive cuisine. Among countless local specialties, Nam O Fish Salad stands out as a culinary symbol, carrying the pure taste of the sea and the simplicity, craftsmanship, and soul of coastal life.

This iconic dish originates from Nam O Fishing Village, located about 15 kilometers north of Da Nang city center. Over generations, Nam O fish salad has become a source of pride for local residents not only for its unique flavor, but also for the story it tells about a life deeply connected to the ocean.

Signature Ingredients – Capturing The Taste Of The Sea

Nam O fish salad is made from simple ingredients, yet it requires extreme freshness and meticulous preparation:

Fresh Herring Fish

Small in size with naturally sweet flesh and soft bones, herring fish is abundant in the waters around Nam O. The fish must be freshly caught on the same day to ensure sweetness and eliminate any fishy taste.

A Variety Of Fresh Herbs

Nam O fish salad is incomplete without an array of fresh herbs such as green banana slices, cucumber, climbing wattle leaves, fish mint, young mango leaves, and lettuce. These herbs not only enhance the flavor but also create a perfect nutritional balance.

Rich And Flavorful Dipping Sauce

The soul of the dish lies in its dipping sauce, made from Nam O fish sauce, a famous local specialty crafted from anchovies. The sauce is blended with garlic, chili, ginger, lime juice, and crushed peanuts, resulting in a bold, spicy, and aromatic flavor that defines Nam O fish salad.

Wet fish salad served with a rich dipping sauce made from traditional Nam O fish sauce.

Preparation Method – The Delicate Craft Of Coastal Locals

Nam O fish salad comes in two versions: dry fish salad and wet fish salad. Each offers a distinct taste experience while preserving the traditional essence.

Step 1: Preparing The Herring

Fresh herring is cleaned, deboned, and thinly sliced. The fish is then marinated with ginger, garlic, chili, and lime juice to neutralize any odor and gently cure the fish.

Step 2: Making Dry Fish Salad

The marinated fish is mixed with roasted rice powder (thinh), which adds a nutty aroma and creamy texture, making the dish more flavorful and appealing.

Step 3: Making Wet Fish Salad

The fish slices are soaked in a diluted mixture of Nam O fish sauce, allowing the fish to absorb the seasoning and develop its signature savory taste.

Step 4: Presentation And Enjoyment

Both versions are served on large plates, surrounded by fresh herbs. The dish is best enjoyed wrapped in rice paper or grilled sesame rice crackers, then dipped into the rich Nam O fish sauce.

A beautifully presented plate of Nam O fish salad with white fish slices, green herbs, and golden roasted rice powder.

Nam O Fish Salad – The Taste Of The Sea And Living Memories

Every bite of Nam O fish salad reflects the essence of the ocean and the dedication of local fishermen. Its unforgettable flavor comes from the harmony of sweet herring fish, nutty roasted rice powder, the slight bitterness of green banana, spicy chili heat, and the fresh aroma of herbs.

More than just a local delicacy, Nam O fish salad represents the pride of the fishing village—a perfect blend of nature, tradition, and love for the homeland shared by generations of coastal residents.

A traditional serving of Nam O fish salad with dipping sauce, evoking the warmth of seaside family meals.

Health Benefits Of Nam O Fish Salad

Beyond its exceptional taste, Nam O fish salad is also a nutritious and healthy dish thanks to its natural ingredients:

Rich In Omega-3

Herring fish is an excellent source of omega-3 fatty acids, supporting heart health, reducing cholesterol, and promoting brain development.

High Fiber Content

Fresh herbs and vegetables provide dietary fiber, aiding digestion and improving gut health.

Low In Calories And Fat

With minimal fat and natural ingredients, this dish is ideal for those maintaining a balanced diet or healthy lifestyle.

Boosts Immunity

Ginger, garlic, and chili not only enhance flavor but also offer anti-inflammatory properties and help strengthen the immune system.

A vibrant plate of Nam O fish salad served with fresh herbs—delicious and nutritious.

Experiencing Nam O Fish Salad At The Fishing Village

To fully appreciate the authentic flavor of Nam O fish salad, visitors should experience it right at Nam O Fishing Village. Sitting by the sea, enjoying fresh fish salad while listening to gentle waves, offers a deeper understanding of why this dish has captivated so many travelers.

More than a meal, Nam O fish salad is a cultural journey—an intimate glimpse into the daily life and traditions of coastal communities during a Da Nang Tour 2026.

A peaceful corner of Nam O Fishing Village, where this legendary dish was born.

Nam O Fish Salad – An Unforgettable Flavor Of Da Nang

Nam O fish salad is not merely a dish; it is a symbol of Da Nang’s coastal culinary heritage. Each bite carries the sweetness of the sea, the fragrance of local herbs, and the honest, rustic spirit of Central Vietnam’s people.

If you have the chance to visit Da Nang, do not miss the opportunity to taste Nam O fish salad. This iconic specialty is not only a culinary highlight but also a bridge connecting travelers to the soul of the sea and the tranquil coastal life of Central Vietnam.

posts.title: Check In At 6 Super Romantic Dating Spots In Da Nang
posts.excerpt: Da Nang is a shining gem of Vietnam’s tourism industry. The city is not only famous for its breathtaking natural landscapes but also stands out for its diverse and attractive tourist destinations. Loc
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang is a shining gem of Vietnam’s tourism industry. The city is not only famous for its breathtaking natural landscapes but also stands out for its diverse and attractive tourist destinations.

Located in Central Vietnam, Da Nang offers a perfect combination of stunning scenery, rich cultural heritage, and modern amenities. For travelers especially couples visiting Da Nang, missing out on its romantic dating spots would be a real loss. Let’s explore with Vietlook Travel the top 6 must-visit romantic check-in locations for couples in the article below.

Top 6 Most Romantic Dating Spots For Travelers In Da Nang

Da Nang is home to many romantic destinations that are ideal for couples. Below are the top 6 most romantic places that visitors should not miss when traveling to Da Nang.

Love Bridge Da Nang

Love Bridge Da Nang, also known as Tran Thi Ly Bridge, is one of the most iconic romantic symbols of the city. Located on Tran Hung Dao Street, the bridge features an elegant design that harmoniously blends modern and traditional architecture. At night, colorful LED lights illuminate the bridge, creating a dazzling and enchanting atmosphere. From here, couples can enjoy breathtaking views of the Han River and Da Nang’s sparkling cityscape, making it a perfect setting for meaningful moments and unforgettable memories of love.

My Khe Beach

My Khe Beach is considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Vietnam and an ideal destination for those seeking a perfect seaside experience. The beach is famous not only for its stunning natural beauty but also for its vibrant recreational and cultural activities. Visitors can enjoy swimming, try various water sports, or simply relax under the shade of coconut trees along the shore. My Khe Beach is not only a top resort destination in Da Nang tours but also a wonderful place for couples to connect with nature and enjoy peaceful, romantic moments by the sea.

Hoi An Ancient Town

Hoi An Ancient Town is a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site located along the Thu Bon River in Quang Nam Province, near Da Nang. With its well-preserved ancient houses, narrow streets, and timeless architecture, Hoi An offers a poetic and nostalgic atmosphere for travelers exploring the Da Nang area. In the evening, the town glows with colorful lanterns and traditional oil lamps, creating a uniquely romantic scene. Cafés, restaurants, and boutique shops come alive, filling the air with culture and charm. Hoi An is not only admired for its historical beauty but also for its rich culinary scene and authentic Vietnamese cultural experiences.

Han River Cruise

A cruise along the Han River is a luxurious and distinctive experience in Da Nang. With lush green riverbanks and panoramic city views, the Han River provides a perfect backdrop for a romantic journey on the water. Travelers joining Da Nang tours can enjoy premium services aboard modern cruise ships, including refined dining experiences and elegant, comfortable spaces. As the boat glides along the river, couples can relax and immerse themselves in the peaceful atmosphere while admiring the sparkling lights from the iconic bridges and riverside landmarks.

Sun World Ba Na Hills

Sun World Ba Na Hills is one of the most famous and unique attractions in Da Nang. Located atop Ba Na Mountain, this destination is renowned for its classic French-inspired architecture, creating a charming and romantic atmosphere. Visitors can experience one of the world’s longest cable car rides, enjoy cool mountain air, and admire the magnificent views overlooking Da Nang city. In addition, Ba Na Hills offers a wide range of entertainment activities, theme parks, and beautiful flower gardens, making it an ideal destination for couples seeking both romance and adventure.

Asia Park

Asia Park is a popular entertainment destination in Da Nang, known for its unique concept and diverse recreational experiences. With its vast area, the park allows visitors to explore architectural styles and cultural elements from various Asian countries. Couples can enjoy modern amusement rides, exciting adventures, and relaxing strolls around the park. In addition, Asia Park features a variety of dining options and vibrant cultural events, making it a lively and enjoyable place for romantic dates.

These destinations promise unforgettable and romantic memories during your time in Da Nang. We hope you and your loved one will enjoy a truly wonderful journey in this beautiful coastal city.

posts.title: Da Nang Travel Tips: What To Buy As Souvenirs For Family And Friends?
posts.excerpt: Da Nang is not only famous for its beautiful landscapes but also a true culinary paradise filled with irresistible local specialties. This article suggests the most unique and meaningful souvenirs you
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang is not only famous for its beautiful landscapes but also a true culinary paradise filled with irresistible local specialties. This article suggests the most unique and meaningful souvenirs you can bring home from your Da Nang trip in 2026 from beef sausage and dried seafood to traditional handicrafts helping you preserve both the flavors and memories of this charming coastal city.

Da Nang, a beautiful seaside city with soft white sand beaches, crystal-clear waters, and rich cuisine, has long been a favorite destination for travelers. When planning your Da Nang trip in 2026, besides sightseeing and enjoying local food, many visitors wonder what souvenirs to buy for friends and family to capture the spirit and memories of Vietnam’s most livable city. Below is a curated list of distinctive local specialties that make perfect gifts guaranteed to delight the recipients and remind them of the sunny, breezy charm of Central Vietnam. Let’s explore together with Vietlook Travel.

Da Nang Travel 2026: What Souvenirs Best Capture the City’s Flavors and Memories?

Da Nang is renowned not only for iconic landmarks such as the Dragon Bridge, Han River Bridge, and My Khe Beach, but also for its rich culinary heritage. Choosing souvenirs from Da Nang is not simply about buying products it’s about bringing home a piece of local culture and tradition. Each gift tells a story, reflecting the coastal lifestyle, culinary craftsmanship, and cultural identity of Central Vietnam. Below are the most popular and meaningful souvenirs you should consider during your Da Nang journey.

1. Da Nang Beef Sausage – A Traditional Flavor to Remember

Beef sausage (cha bo) is one of the most famous specialties of Da Nang and Central Vietnam. Unlike regular pork sausage, Da Nang beef sausage is made from carefully selected fresh beef, finely ground and seasoned with traditional spices such as pepper, garlic, and premium fish sauce. The mixture is wrapped in fresh banana leaves and steamed, creating a distinctive aroma and firm, chewy texture.

When tasted, the natural sweetness of beef blends perfectly with a mild peppery kick, delivering a memorable flavor. Beef sausage is not only delicious but also an elegant and symbolic gift representing Da Nang cuisine. Choose sausages with a natural light pink color, smooth surface, and a gentle beef aroma. Prices range from 200,000 to 350,000 VND per kilogram. You can buy high-quality beef sausage at Con Market, Han Market, or reputable specialty shops such as Ba Tam or Song Han.

2. One-Sun-Dried Squid – The Essence of the Sea

One-sun-dried squid is a premium seafood delicacy that embodies the essence of Da Nang’s coastal flavor. Fresh squid is dried under the sun for just one day, preserving its natural sweetness, tenderness, and ocean aroma unlike fully dried squid.

When grilled or pan-fried, the squid becomes fragrant, slightly chewy, and irresistibly delicious, making it perfect for family gatherings or casual snacking. One-sun-dried squid is a refined and popular souvenir among travelers. Choose squid with a natural pink color, thick body, and a light white powder on the surface. Prices range from 500,000 to 1,000,000 VND per kilogram. For the best quality, buy from trusted dried seafood stores or fishing villages such as Nam O or Thanh Khe.

3. Tamarind-Rimmed Baby Squid – Sweet and Tangy Delight

Tamarind-rimmed baby squid is a beloved Da Nang specialty, featuring tender baby squid simmered in a sweet-and-sour tamarind sauce. Fresh squid is carefully cleaned and cooked with tamarind juice, sugar, chili, and spices until the sauce thickens and coats each piece evenly.

The result is a flavorful snack with a perfect balance of sweetness, tanginess, and mild spice. This dish is easy to store and transport, making it an ideal souvenir. Prices typically range from 150,000 to 250,000 VND per box and are available at specialty stores and supermarkets.

4. Spicy Dried Filefish – A Savory Snack Favorite

Spicy dried filefish (ca bo kho rim) is another iconic seafood snack from Da Nang. Fresh filefish is dried naturally, then simmered with chili, garlic, sugar, and fish sauce until fully infused with flavor.

With its chewy texture, balanced sweet-salty taste, and spicy kick, this snack is perfect for casual munching or as a gift for seafood lovers. Easy to preserve and carry, dried filefish costs around 180,000–300,000 VND per 500g bag.

5. Nam O Fish Sauce – A Culinary Heritage

Nam O fish sauce is a proud symbol of Da Nang’s traditional cuisine. Produced in the ancient fishing village of Nam O, this fish sauce is made entirely by hand using fresh anchovies and sea salt, fermented naturally in clay jars over many months.

The result is a deep amber-colored sauce with a rich aroma, balanced salinity, and lingering aftertaste. Nam O fish sauce elevates Vietnamese dishes and represents the cultural heritage of coastal Da Nang. Prices range from 80,000 to 150,000 VND per liter, depending on protein content.

6. My Khe Seaweed – A Healthy Gift from the Ocean

Harvested from My Khe Beach one of the most beautiful beaches in the world My Khe seaweed is fresh, nutritious, and rich in minerals. It’s commonly used in soups, salads, and traditional dishes, offering both health benefits and authentic coastal flavor.

Dried My Khe seaweed costs approximately 50,000–100,000 VND per 200g pack and makes an excellent gift for health-conscious friends and family.

7. Peanut Candy – A Sweet Taste of Central Vietnam

Peanut candy is a traditional Central Vietnamese sweet made from roasted peanuts and malt sugar. Crispy, fragrant, and mildly sweet, it pairs perfectly with hot tea and evokes nostalgic childhood memories.

Handmade and affordable, peanut candy is a popular souvenir priced at around 30,000–60,000 VND per pack.
