8. Ba Lieu Sesame Crackers – Traditional Culinary Craftsmanship

Ba Lieu sesame crackers are one of Da Nang’s most iconic traditional treats. Made from glutinous rice flour, sugar, ginger, and roasted sesame seeds, the crackers are crispy on the outside and light, aromatic inside, with a subtle gingery warmth.

Priced between 40,000 and 80,000 VND per box, they are a meaningful gift reflecting the craftsmanship and culinary heritage of Da Nang.

9. Specialty Tea and Coffee – Unique Local Beverages

Although not a major tea- or coffee-growing region, Da Nang is a hub for specialty products from nearby areas such as Quang Nam and the Central Highlands. Visitors can find herbal teas, lotus tea, butterfly pea flower tea, and high-quality roasted coffee.

Salt coffee, a unique local variation, offers a fascinating blend of mild saltiness, bitterness, and creamy sweetness. Tea and coffee gifts typically range from 100,000 to 300,000 VND per pack.

10. Handicraft Souvenirs – Cultural Imprints of Da Nang

Beyond food, Da Nang offers a wide range of handicrafts such as hand-painted conical hats, ceramic items, and stone carvings from the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son). These souvenirs reflect local artistry and cultural identity, with prices ranging from a few dollars to several hundred thousand VND depending on craftsmanship.

Smart Shopping Tips for Buying Da Nang Specialties

  • Choose reputable shopping spots: Con Market, Han Market, specialty stores, supermarkets, or airport shops.

  • Check packaging and expiration dates, especially for food products.

  • Bargain politely at traditional markets.

  • Buy moderate quantities and request vacuum sealing for dried seafood.

  • Ask locals for recommendations to find the best quality products.

  • Shop early in the morning for the freshest goods.

  • Consider transport conditions, especially for items requiring refrigeration.

Central Vietnamese cuisine, especially Da Nang’s, is incredibly diverse and appealing. This curated list by Vietlook Travel will help you choose meaningful and delicious souvenirs for your loved ones. We hope these suggestions make your Da Nang trip even more fulfilling and memorable. Happy travels and enjoy discovering the flavors of Da Nang.

posts.title: Discover 6 Famous Delicious – Affordable When Traveling To Da Nang
posts.excerpt: Da Nang is a true food paradise with countless unique local delicacies. This article introduces six well-known dining spots that are delicious, affordable, and highly rated by both locals and traveler
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang is a true food paradise with countless unique local delicacies. This article introduces six well-known dining spots that are delicious, affordable, and highly rated by both locals and travelers from Ba Duong’s banh xeo and Hon fish cake noodle soup to Trang Kitchen’s frog Mi Quang along with useful tips to help you enjoy a complete culinary journey in Da Nang in 2026.

Da Nang, the most livable city in Vietnam, is famous not only for its turquoise beaches and modern lifestyle but also for its rich and diverse culinary scene. Each local dish reflects the region’s culture, from humble street food to refined restaurant cuisine. If you’re planning a trip to Da Nang in 2026, don’t miss the opportunity to explore these iconic local flavors at six must-visit food spots below. This promises to be an unforgettable gastronomic journey, offering deeper insight into Da Nang’s people and culture through every bite.

6 Must Try Food Destinations for an Authentic Da Nang Culinary Experience

To fully enjoy Da Nang’s cuisine, choosing the right dining spots is essential. Below are six popular eateries highly praised by locals and visitors alike for their flavor, quality, and reasonable prices—perfect even for the most discerning food lovers.

1. Ba Duong Banh Xeo – A Traditional Flavor You Can’t Miss

Ba Duong Banh Xeo is an iconic culinary landmark in Da Nang, welcoming thousands of visitors daily. Tucked away in a small alley, the eatery offers a cozy, authentic street-food atmosphere. What makes Ba Duong’s banh xeo special is its golden, crispy shell that’s never greasy, filled generously with fresh shrimp, pork belly, and bean sprouts.

The soul of the dish lies in its signature dipping sauce, made from a secret family recipe featuring pork liver, peanuts, chili, and a perfectly balanced sweet-and-sour taste. Wrap the crispy pancake with fresh herbs and dip it generously into the sauce for a truly unforgettable flavor experience. Each banh xeo costs around 20,000–30,000 VND, making it perfect for a light meal or a filling lunch.

Address: K280/23 Hoang Dieu Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang

2. Ba Doi Banh Canh – A Unique Self-Seasoning Experience

Ba Doi Banh Canh offers not just delicious food but a unique dining experience. Here, guests are served a simple bowl of thick noodle soup with chewy noodles, fresh shrimp, and fish cake, accompanied by a tray of seasonings so you can adjust the flavor to your personal taste.

The broth, simmered from bones and seafood, has a naturally sweet and delicate flavor. Adding salt, chili, MSG, and scallion oil allows each diner to customize their bowl. Open from early morning until evening, it’s an excellent choice for breakfast or an afternoon meal. Prices range from 25,000–40,000 VND per bowl.

Address: 263 Khuc Hao Street, Nai Hien Dong Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang

3. Hon Fish Cake Noodle Soup – A Flavorful Taste of the Sea

Hon Fish Cake Noodle Soup is a favorite breakfast spot for both locals and tourists. The restaurant is famous for its fish cake noodle soup but also serves tuna noodle soup, mackerel noodle soup, and crab noodle soup.

The highlight is the naturally sweet broth made from fish bones and vegetables, delivering a true ocean-inspired flavor. The fish cakes are made from fresh fish, offering a firm yet tender texture. A hot bowl of noodles with chili paste and fresh herbs is the perfect way to start a day of exploring Da Nang. Prices range from 30,000–45,000 VND per bowl.

Address: 86 Quang Trung Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang

4. Frog Mi Quang at Bep Trang – A Signature Local Specialty

Bep Trang is one of the most famous names in Da Nang cuisine, especially known for its unique frog Mi Quang. The frog meat is stir-fried with traditional spices, creating a rich, aromatic flavor. Combined with chewy rice noodles, thick savory broth, fresh herbs, and crispy sesame rice crackers, the dish is both visually appealing and delicious.

Many travelers say that visiting Da Nang without trying Bep Trang’s Mi Quang is like missing a key part of the city’s food culture. The spacious, airy restaurant is ideal for families and groups. A bowl costs around 45,000–60,000 VND.

Address: 441 Ong Ich Khiem Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang

5. Ro Cau Mong Veal – A Quintessential Quang Region Delicacy

Cau Mong veal is a famous specialty of Quang Nam, and in Da Nang, Ro Cau Mong Veal serves an authentic version of this beloved dish. The veal is flame-roasted whole using straw or charcoal, preserving its tenderness, natural sweetness, and appealing pink color. The crispy skin and juicy meat are best enjoyed with the restaurant’s signature fermented fish sauce (mam nem), slightly spicy and deeply flavorful.

The restaurant also serves stir-fried noodles and hot pot, making it a great spot for family meals or casual gatherings. Prices range from 150,000–300,000 VND per plate, depending on portion size.

Address: 8 Bac Son Street, Cam Le District, Da Nang

6. Ba Tu Rice Paper Snacks – Simple but Addictive Street Food

Ba Tu’s banh trang dap and banh trang with dipping sauce are popular street snacks that perfectly represent Da Nang’s food culture. The dish combines crispy grilled rice paper with soft steamed rice paper, minced meat, quail eggs, and fried shallots, lightly pressed together and dipped in the shop’s special soy sauce.

The sauce, with its balanced salty-sweet flavor and mild chili kick, makes this simple dish incredibly addictive. Always crowded from morning to night, the shop proves how irresistible this snack is. Prices range from just 15,000–25,000 VND per plate.

Address: 354 Le Duan Street, Hai Chau District, Da Nang

Tips for an Efficient Da Nang Food Adventure

  • Best time to visit: Da Nang can be visited year-round, but the dry season from February to August offers the best weather for food exploration.

  • Transportation: Renting a motorbike (100,000–150,000 VND/day) is the most convenient way to explore food spots. Taxis and ride-hailing apps are also reliable options.

  • Budget: Most local dishes cost between 20,000–60,000 VND, making Da Nang an affordable food destination.

  • Food culture: Be open to trying new dishes and chatting with locals—they’re often happy to share food stories and recommendations.

  • Food safety: Choose busy, popular eateries to ensure freshness and quality.

Conclusion

Da Nang is not only a captivating travel destination but also a true culinary haven. From crispy banh xeo and customizable banh canh to flavorful fish cake noodles, unique frog Mi Quang, tender roasted veal, and humble rice paper snacks, each dish tells a story about the region’s culture and people. With these six famous food spots and practical tips, we hope your culinary adventure in Da Nang in 2026 will be truly unforgettable.

posts.title: Discover Dragon Bridge – A Must Visit Nightlife Hotspot In Da Nang
posts.excerpt: Dragon Bridge Da Nang, an iconic architectural landmark famous for its spectacular fire and water shows, is a destination you simply can’t miss. This article provides detailed information about its hi
posts.contentHtml:
Dragon Bridge Da Nang, an iconic architectural landmark famous for its spectacular fire and water shows, is a destination you simply can’t miss. This article provides detailed information about its history, architecture, transportation, ideal visiting time, and helpful travel tips to ensure a complete and memorable experience. Let’s explore the dazzling beauty and profound meaning of Dragon Bridge in the heart of Da Nang.

Da Nang, known as the most livable city in Vietnam, is not only famous for its stunning beaches and rich culinary scene but also impresses visitors with its unique system of bridges spanning the Han River. Each bridge has its own charm and significance, but the most outstanding of all is Dragon Bridge – an architectural masterpiece and a highlight of any Da Nang travel tour. With its majestic dragon-shaped design, Dragon Bridge is not only a vital traffic route but also a symbol of prosperity and the city’s aspiration to rise and reach out to the world. Join Vietlook Travel as we explore the beauty, history, and exciting experiences that Dragon Bridge offers on your journey through Da Nang.

An Overview of Dragon Bridge Da Nang

Dragon Bridge is the sixth bridge crossing the Han River and features a unique design inspired by the Ly Dynasty dragon, stretching powerfully toward the sea. Construction began in 2009, and the bridge was officially inaugurated on March 29, 2013, in celebration of the 38th anniversary of Da Nang’s liberation. Measuring 666 meters in length and 37.5 meters in width, the bridge includes six traffic lanes and two pedestrian walkways, conveniently connecting Hai Chau District and Son Tra District.

What truly sets Dragon Bridge apart is its ability to breathe fire and spray water on weekend nights, attracting thousands of locals and tourists alike. This impressive performance reflects architectural creativity and carries deep cultural meaning, symbolizing strength, prosperity, and Da Nang’s ambition for growth. In Asian culture, the dragon represents power and good fortune, and the image of the bridge breathing fire and water serves as a warm welcome to visitors from all over the world. This is truly an unmissable experience when visiting this beautiful coastal city.

The Unique Architecture of Dragon Bridge

Dragon Bridge is not merely a transportation structure but a remarkable work of architectural art. Its design is inspired by the Ly Dynasty dragon, a powerful symbol in Vietnamese culture. The dragon’s head faces the East Sea, representing Da Nang’s aspiration to expand globally. The dragon’s sinuous body stretches across 666 meters and is coated in a shimmering golden color, creating a radiant appearance by day and a magical glow at night.

The bridge features an advanced lighting system with nearly 2,500 LED lights capable of changing colors, creating stunning visual displays. Most notably, the fire- and water-breathing technology installed in the dragon’s head captivates millions of visitors. This unique combination of engineering and art also carries feng shui significance, symbolizing prosperity and good fortune. Dragon Bridge has received numerous international architectural awards, affirming its status as one of the most beautiful and unique bridges in the world.

How to Get to Dragon Bridge in Da Nang

Located in the city center on Nguyen Van Linh Street, Dragon Bridge is extremely easy to access from anywhere in Da Nang.

From Da Nang International Airport:
The bridge is about 3–4 km away. Taxis, ride-hailing services (Grab, Gojek), or public buses are all convenient options. Travel time is approximately 10–15 minutes depending on traffic.

From Da Nang Railway Station:
The station is around 2–3 km from Dragon Bridge. Taxis or ride-hailing services are the most convenient choices.

From Hoi An:
Visitors can take public buses for an economical daytime option, then transfer to a taxi or walk a short distance. Renting a motorbike is also a great choice for flexibility. From Hoi An, follow the coastal road, then turn onto Vo Van Kiet Street to reach Dragon Bridge.

From Da Nang city center:
From central hotels, simply follow Vo Nguyen Giap Street, turn left onto Vo Van Kiet Street, and continue straight. Walking is also an enjoyable option, allowing you to admire the Han River scenery.

Best Time to Visit and Entrance Fees

The best time to visit Dragon Bridge is in the evening, especially on Saturday and Sunday nights. At 9:00 PM, the bridge performs its famous fire and water show, lasting about 15 minutes. The bridge lights up brilliantly, creating a breathtaking scene. It’s recommended to arrive around 8:30 PM to secure a good viewing spot.

Visiting Dragon Bridge is completely free. However, additional experiences such as Han River cruises or rooftop cafés nearby may involve extra costs. Cruise tickets typically range from 100,000 to 200,000 VND per person, while rooftop cafés charge around 50,000–150,000 VND per drink.

Best Spots to Watch Dragon Bridge

To fully enjoy the fire and water show at 9:00 PM on weekends, consider these ideal viewing locations:

  • On the bridge itself: Traffic is stopped during the show, allowing visitors to stand directly on the bridge for the most immersive experience.

  • Bach Dang Walking Street: Located at the end of the bridge, offering a full panoramic view along with nearby restaurants and cafés.

  • Rooftop cafés and nearby hotels: Places like Novotel Danang Premier Han River or A La Carte Danang Beach Hotel provide elevated views and a more private atmosphere.

  • Nearby bridges: Tran Thi Ly Bridge and Han River Bridge offer unique perspectives, especially when Han River Bridge rotates at night.

  • Tran Hung Dao Street: Runs along the eastern bank of the Han River, offering clear, unobstructed views.

  • Han River cruise: A romantic and memorable way to watch the show from the water while enjoying dinner.

Handy Tips for a Perfect Da Nang Trip

  • Reserve in advance: Book riverside restaurants or rooftop cafés early, especially on weekends.

  • Check show schedules: While the show usually takes place at 9:00 PM on weekends, minor changes may occur.

  • Bring a camera: The fire and water show offers fantastic photo opportunities.

  • Explore Da Nang nightlife: After the show, enjoy local night food such as Mi Quang, fish cake noodle soup, banh xeo, or fresh seafood.

  • Combine nearby attractions: Visit Son Tra Night Market, Asia Park, or the Cham Museum for a well-rounded itinerary.

The Meaning of Dragon Bridge to the People of Da Nang

To the people of Da Nang, Dragon Bridge is more than just an architectural structure it is a symbol of pride and progress. The bridge has transformed the city’s image, helping Da Nang evolve into a vibrant and modern tourist destination. The dragon breathing fire and water represents strength, ambition, and the relentless spirit of the local people.

Dragon Bridge also hosts major cultural events and festivals, making it a lively gathering place for both locals and tourists. It has become a beloved spot for leisure, entertainment, and romantic evenings. Every performance brings a lively, energetic atmosphere that reflects the youthful and dynamic rhythm of Da Nang.

Above is a comprehensive and detailed guide to Dragon Bridge Da Nang compiled by Vietlook Travel. We hope this information gives you deeper insight into this iconic landmark and provides useful tips for your upcoming Da Nang travel tour. Wishing you a joyful journey filled with unforgettable experiences in this beautiful coastal city

posts.title: Discover The Street Food Paradise At Con Market In Your Da Nang Tour
posts.excerpt: Con Market in Da Nang is not only one of the city’s most vibrant traditional markets but also a true paradise for street food lovers. Here, travelers can explore a wide variety of local specialties, f
posts.contentHtml:
Con Market in Da Nang is not only one of the city’s most vibrant traditional markets but also a true paradise for street food lovers. Here, travelers can explore a wide variety of local specialties, from pork wrapped in rice paper and spicy snail dishes to Mi Quang noodles and refreshing sweet soups. In addition to its rich culinary scene, Con Market is also an ideal place to shop for souvenirs and high-quality dried seafood.

Located in the heart of the city, Con Market has long been a cultural and culinary icon of Da Nang. More than just a bustling trading hub, it offers visitors an immersive experience into Central Vietnam’s street food culture, where each dish reflects the region’s traditions and local lifestyle. Let’s take a closer look at this culinary heaven and the unique experiences it offers during your Da Nang journey.

Location And Opening Hours Of Con Market Da Nang

Con Market is located at 290 Hung Vuong Street, Vinh Trung Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang. Thanks to its central location, visitors can easily reach the market by taxi, motorbike, or even on foot if staying nearby.

The market opens from 7:00 AM daily and features more than 2,000 stalls, spread across a three-story building, two two-story wings, and several ground-level market areas.

For the best experience, visitors are recommended to come in the late afternoon or early evening, when the food area becomes liveliest and the aroma of freshly cooked dishes fills the air. Most food stalls begin closing around 7:30 PM, but many eateries around the market remain open late, offering additional dining options.

A Culinary Journey Through Con Market Da Nang

Con Market is not just a traditional market it is a living culinary museum of Da Nang. Every dish here tells a story, showcasing the flavors, culture, and character of Central Vietnam. When joining a Da Nang tour, stepping into Con Market means entering a world of unforgettable tastes.

Pork Wrapped In Rice Paper – A Must-Try Specialty

Pork wrapped in rice paper is one of Da Nang’s most iconic dishes. It is loved for its simple yet perfectly balanced combination of fresh ingredients. Thinly sliced boiled pork belly, cooked just right, retains its natural sweetness and tender texture. It is served with a generous plate of fresh herbs such as lettuce, fish mint, basil, cucumber, green mango, and pineapple.

The highlight of this dish is mam nem, a fermented anchovy dipping sauce made with garlic, chili, sugar, lime, and crushed pineapple. Its bold, aromatic, sweet-and-spicy flavor brings all ingredients together. One bite of a well-wrapped roll dipped in mam nem delivers an explosion of flavors that visitors are sure to remember long after leaving Da Nang.

Spicy Snails – An Addictive Street Snack

Spicy snails, locally known as oc mut, are among the most popular snacks at Con Market. Small snails are stir-fried with lemongrass and chili, creating a fragrant, slightly spicy, sweet-and-savory dish. The fun lies in gently sucking the snail meat out of its shell, enjoying its chewy texture mixed with rich sauce.

These snails are often served with pickled vegetables, whose sourness perfectly balances the spiciness of the dish. Fresh ingredients and skillful preparation make this snack a favorite among both locals and travelers exploring Da Nang.

Grilled Pork Sticky Rice – A Comforting Breakfast

Grilled pork sticky rice is a beloved breakfast dish in Da Nang. Though simple, it is deeply satisfying. Sticky rice is soft and fragrant, topped with marinated pork grilled over charcoal until golden and aromatic.

The juicy grilled meat combined with warm sticky rice and a sprinkle of roasted sesame seeds creates a comforting and filling meal. If you visit Con Market in the morning, this dish is highly recommended for an authentic local start to the day.

Mi Quang – The Essence Of Quang Cuisine

No culinary journey in Da Nang is complete without Mi Quang. At Con Market, many family-run stalls serve authentic versions of this iconic dish. Thick rice noodles are topped with rich broth made from simmered bones, shrimp, pork, chicken, quail eggs, and fish cakes.

Mi Quang is always served with fresh herbs and crispy sesame rice crackers, creating a beautiful balance of textures and flavors. Each bowl is a colorful and flavorful reflection of Central Vietnam’s culinary heritage.

Bun Mam Nem – A Bold Central Vietnamese Flavor

Bun mam nem is a rustic yet highly popular dish in Da Nang. The star of this dish is its fermented anchovy sauce, mixed with garlic, chili, sugar, and pineapple, creating a strong, aromatic flavor.

Fresh rice vermicelli is combined with sliced boiled pork, fermented pork rolls, beef sausage, pig ears, and fresh vegetables. Once mixed together, the dish delivers a harmonious blend of salty, sweet, spicy, sour, and refreshing flavors. Affordable and filling, bun mam nem is a must-try for adventurous food lovers.

Sweet Soups – A Refreshing Dessert Finale

After enjoying savory dishes, visitors should stop by the dessert area for a refreshing bowl of Vietnamese sweet soup (che). Con Market offers a wide variety, including mung bean sweet soup, corn sweet soup, lotus seed sweet soup, taro sweet soup, banana sweet soup, and the famous mixed fruit sweet soup with coconut milk.

These desserts are lightly sweetened, cooling, and perfect for ending a food tour. Prices are very reasonable, usually around 10,000–20,000 VND per cup.

Useful Tips When Visiting Con Market Da Nang

  • Best time to visit: Late afternoon to early evening (4:00 PM – 7:00 PM) for the most vibrant food scene.

  • Transportation: Easy access by walking, motorbike, taxi, or bus. Parking areas are available nearby.

  • Pricing: Food is affordable, but it is still recommended to ask prices before ordering.

  • Food safety: Choose stalls that look clean and attract many customers.

  • Crowds: The market can be busy and noisy during peak hours, so be prepared for a lively atmosphere.

What To Buy As Souvenirs From Con Market?

Dried Seafood

Con Market is famous for dried fish, dried shrimp, and dried squid. These products are high-quality, flavorful, and easy to pack, making them perfect gifts from Da Nang.

Rimmed Squid

Sweet and spicy rimmed squid is a favorite snack and souvenir. It is well-seasoned, chewy, and available in convenient packaging.

Beef Sausage

Da Nang beef sausage is well-known for its pure beef flavor and firm texture. It is ideal as a gift or to enjoy with noodles or bread.

Handicrafts And Souvenirs

Visitors can also find small handicrafts such as keychains, conical hats, woven bags, and decorative items meaningful souvenirs that reflect local culture.

Con Market is more than just a place to eat or shop it is a cultural heartbeat of Da Nang, offering the most authentic glimpse into local life. With its diverse cuisine, lively atmosphere, and cultural value, Con Market is truly a must-visit destination on any Da Nang tour.

posts.title: Independent Travel In Da Nang In Autumn
posts.excerpt: In autumn 2026, Da Nang embraces a romantic and gentle charm, making it an ideal time to explore this vibrant coastal city. Travelers can enjoy fresh air, stunning scenery, and diverse local cuisine a
posts.contentHtml:
In autumn 2026, Da Nang embraces a romantic and gentle charm, making it an ideal time to explore this vibrant coastal city. Travelers can enjoy fresh air, stunning scenery, and diverse local cuisine at more affordable costs compared to the peak season.

Autumn, with its mild weather and refreshing atmosphere, has always been a perfect time to discover new destinations. And when it comes to autumn travel, Da Nang appears like a poetic painting, graceful and unexpectedly romantic. Gone is the scorching summer heat, and the winter chill has yet to arrive. Instead, Da Nang in autumn offers a calm, crisp, and soothing ambiance. Early morning mist softly blankets the city, adding a dreamy touch to its coastal beauty.

Visiting Da Nang in autumn 2026 allows travelers to bask in golden sunsets, admire the city’s serene landscapes, and enjoy unforgettable experiences at a relaxed pace. Let’s explore the most attractive destinations in Da Nang during this enchanting autumn season.

The Beauty Of Autumn Weather In Da Nang

Da Nang has a tropical monsoon climate with two main seasons: the dry season and the rainy season. Autumn, from September to November, marks the transition into the rainy period. However, this does not mean constant rain or unpleasant weather. Instead, Da Nang reveals a unique charm, with clear sunny days alternating with light, brief showers, creating a cool, poetic atmosphere.

Average temperatures range from 22°C to 28°C, making it ideal for sightseeing, walking tours, and street food exploration. Occasional rain showers help refresh the air and add a romantic mood to the city. Compared to summer, transportation is more convenient and less crowded. Travelers can easily rent motorbikes or use taxis and ride-hailing services at reasonable prices.

Another major advantage of visiting Da Nang in autumn is the lower cost of services. Flights, hotels, tours, and dining prices are generally more affordable, allowing visitors to enjoy high-quality experiences while saving money. This season also offers more opportunities to connect with friendly locals and experience Da Nang at a slower, more authentic pace.

Must-Visit Places For Independent Travel In Da Nang In Autumn 2026

Autumn brings a fresh perspective to Da Nang, making familiar destinations feel new and captivating. Below are top recommendations for your independent autumn journey.

Ba Na Hills – A Fairytale Autumn Escape

Ba Na Hills is always a top attraction in Da Nang, and in autumn, it becomes even more magical. Thanks to its elevation, Ba Na Hills enjoys cool weather year-round, but autumn adds misty layers that transform the area into a fairytale-like landscape.

Taking the cable car early in the morning, when fog still lingers, is an unforgettable experience. From above, travelers can admire Da Nang hidden among clouds. Highlights include the French Village with its European architecture, the colorful Le Jardin D’Amour flower gardens, and the iconic Golden Bridge.

Autumn sees fewer visitors, allowing more freedom to explore, take photos, and enjoy attractions like Fantasy Park without long waits. Seasonal promotions on cable car tickets and accommodation also make Ba Na Hills a cost-effective yet rewarding experience.

Son Tra Peninsula – The Green Jewel Of Da Nang

Known as the “green lung” of Da Nang, Son Tra Peninsula offers untouched natural beauty and breathtaking landscapes. Although autumn may not be ideal for swimming due to occasional rain, it is perfect for nature exploration and scenic drives.

Winding coastal roads surrounded by lush greenery become especially poetic under soft autumn sunlight and morning mist. Visitors can stop at Linh Ung Pagoda to admire the tallest Lady Buddha statue in Vietnam and enjoy panoramic views of the city. Other highlights include the historic Tien Sa Lighthouse and the ancient banyan tree.

The calm atmosphere of autumn makes Son Tra an excellent destination for picnics, light trekking, or simply relaxing while breathing in fresh sea air—a meaningful way to reconnect with nature.

Con Market And Han Market – Food And Shopping Paradise

Rainy autumn days are perfect for exploring Da Nang’s most famous markets: Con Market and Han Market. Both offer sheltered spaces, allowing visitors to shop and dine comfortably regardless of the weather.

Con Market is famous for its affordable street food, including banh xeo, nem lui, bun mam nem, and various local desserts. Han Market is ideal for purchasing dried seafood, fish sauce, local specialties, fabrics, and souvenirs.

Da Nang is well known for its honest pricing and friendly vendors, making shopping here a pleasant and stress-free experience.

Hoi An Ancient Town – Timeless Beauty

No trip to Da Nang is complete without a visit to Hoi An Ancient Town, located about 30 kilometers away. Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Hoi An is famous for its preserved architecture, lantern-lit streets, and peaceful atmosphere.

Autumn is one of the best times to explore Hoi An, with cooler weather and fewer tourists. Visitors can stroll through narrow streets, visit landmarks such as the Japanese Covered Bridge, ancient houses, and assembly halls, or enjoy coffee at charming riverside cafés.

In the evening, colorful lanterns illuminate the town, creating a magical setting. Releasing lanterns on the Hoai River is a meaningful cultural experience symbolizing peace and good fortune.

Marble Mountains – Spiritual And Natural Wonders

The Marble Mountains, also known as Ngu Hanh Son, are a cluster of five limestone and marble hills, each representing one of the five elements. This destination combines dramatic natural scenery with deep spiritual significance.

Autumn’s mild weather is ideal for exploring caves, pagodas, and viewpoints. Thuy Son, the largest and most popular mountain, features impressive caves such as Huyen Khong Cave and historic temples like Tam Thai Pagoda. From the summit, visitors can enjoy panoramic views of Non Nuoc Beach and the surrounding countryside.

Dragon Bridge And Love Bridge – Modern Icons Of Da Nang

Da Nang also impresses with its modern architecture. Dragon Bridge, spanning the Han River, is especially spectacular on weekend evenings when it breathes fire and water at 9:00 PM.

Nearby, Love Bridge offers a romantic setting with thousands of love locks placed by couples. It is a peaceful spot for evening walks, photography, and enjoying riverside cafés with beautiful views.

Autumn Cuisine In Da Nang – Unforgettable Flavors

Autumn weather is perfect for enjoying Da Nang’s warm, flavorful dishes:

  • Mi Quang: Thick rice noodles with rich broth, shrimp, pork, quail eggs, and fresh herbs.

  • Bun Cha Ca: Fish cake noodle soup with light, sweet broth.

  • Fresh Seafood: Available year-round at local markets and seaside restaurants.

  • Banh Xeo And Nem Lui: Crispy pancakes and grilled pork skewers, perfect for cool evenings.

Travel Tips For Visiting Da Nang In Autumn 2026

  • Clothing: Bring light jackets and umbrellas for cooler mornings and unexpected rain.

  • Booking: Reserve flights and hotels early for better deals.

  • Transportation: Motorbike rentals are popular, but taxis and ride-hailing apps are safer during rainy days.

  • Weather Check: Monitor forecasts to adjust your itinerary if needed.

  • Local Interaction: Engage with locals for travel tips and cultural insights.

Autumn is truly the perfect season to experience a peaceful, romantic, and authentic Da Nang. With its gentle climate, rich cuisine, and diverse attractions, Da Nang in autumn 2026 promises a memorable journey filled with beauty and relaxation.

posts.title: Recommended Best Hotels For Travelers Visiting Da Nang
posts.excerpt: To enjoy a truly fulfilling trip to Da Nang, choosing the right hotel that fits your budget while still ensuring quality service is extremely important. In this article, Du Lich Viet shares useful tip
posts.contentHtml:
To enjoy a truly fulfilling trip to Da Nang, choosing the right hotel that fits your budget while still ensuring quality service is extremely important. In this article, Du Lich Viet shares useful tips and recommends the top 5 best hotels in Da Nang, guaranteeing an exceptional stay for your 2026 vacation.

Da Nang, a beautiful coastal city with smooth white sand beaches, the poetic Han River, and rich local cuisine, has long been a favorite destination for both domestic and international travelers. A comfortable, well-equipped hotel will help you recharge after a full day of exploration and elevate your overall travel experience.

Why Is Choosing a Quality Hotel Important When Traveling to Da Nang?

A good hotel is more than just a place to sleep it plays a key role in shaping your entire trip. A high-quality hotel offers several significant benefits.

First, a prime location helps save time and transportation costs. Imagine being able to walk to the iconic Dragon Bridge, easily travel to Ba Na Hills or Hoi An Ancient Town without hassle especially important for families with children or travelers on a tight schedule.

Second, modern facilities and amenities are essential. After a long day of sightseeing, relaxing by an infinity pool, enjoying a professional spa treatment, or dining at an on-site restaurant helps restore your energy and turns your vacation into a truly memorable experience.

Finally, professional service and a comfortable atmosphere determine guest satisfaction. Attentive staff can assist with tour bookings, dining recommendations, and special requests. A thoughtfully designed space offers a cozy, home-like feeling—even while you’re far from home.

Criteria for Choosing a Hotel in Da Nang

To make your Da Nang trip unforgettable, consider the following key factors when selecting accommodation:

Strategic Location

  • Beachfront areas such as My Khe Beach or Pham Van Dong Street offer relaxation and easy access to the sea.

  • City center areas near the Han River and Dragon Bridge are ideal for sightseeing, nightlife, and street food exploration.

Accommodation Type & Budget

Da Nang offers everything from budget homestays and boutique hotels to luxury 5-star resorts. Define your budget early and check online platforms or contact hotels directly for promotions.

Facilities & Services

Look for amenities such as swimming pools (especially infinity pools), spas, gyms, restaurants, airport transfers, and children’s play areas for family travelers.

Guest Reviews

Always read reviews on reputable booking platforms to gain insight into service quality, cleanliness, and staff attitude.

Flexible Cancellation Policy

Flexible cancellation or change policies are important, especially when travel plans may change unexpectedly.

Top 5 Best Hotels in Da Nang with Premium Amenities

1. Melia Riverfront Da Nang – Million-Dollar View Over the Han River

Formerly Vinpearl Danang Riverfront, this luxurious 5-star hotel sits in the heart of the city with panoramic views of the Han River, Dragon Bridge, and My Khe Beach. Its location is ideal for exploring nearby attractions such as Hoi An Ancient Town, My Son Sanctuary, and Hue Imperial City.

Rooms are modern and well-equipped, offering either city or river views. Highlights include a rooftop infinity pool, three high-end restaurants serving Asian and Western cuisine, a stylish bar, spa services, and a modern fitness center. Perfect for couples and families seeking elegance and comfort.

2. Chicland Hotel Da Nang – A Green Oasis in the City

Chicland Hotel stands out with its eco-friendly architecture, featuring lush greenery from ground level to rooftop. Each room is uniquely designed using sustainable materials, creating a fresh and tranquil atmosphere.

Located just steps from My Khe Beach, Chicland is ideal for travelers who appreciate nature-inspired design and responsible tourism. Facilities include an outdoor pool, a restaurant using local ingredients, and a green café. Cultural activities are often organized for guests interested in local traditions.

3. Paracel Hotel Da Nang – Luxury and Relaxation by the Sea

Situated in Son Tra District near My Khe Beach, Paracel Hotel features a modern design with elegant interiors. Rooms are soundproofed and fully equipped with large TVs, minibars, and safes.

Guests can enjoy a premium spa with a jacuzzi, sauna, and professional massage services. The on-site restaurant and bar serve fresh local seafood and international dishes. The hotel is conveniently located near Han Market, Han River Bridge, Cham Museum, and Da Nang International Airport.

4. Grand Sea Hotel Da Nang – Ideal for Family Travelers

Grand Sea Hotel offers a warm, family-friendly atmosphere with spacious rooms and family suites. The large swimming pool is perfect for children and adults alike, while the breakfast buffet includes both Asian and Western options.

Its location provides easy access to popular attractions such as the Han River Bridge and marina areas. Airport transfers and local tour services are available, making it convenient for families planning excursions.

5. Belle Maison Parosand Da Nang – Charming Stay by My Khe Beach

Located directly along My Khe Beach, Belle Maison Parosand offers stunning ocean views and professional service. Rooms overlook the sea, allowing guests to enjoy sunrise and sunset from their balconies.

The rooftop pool is a standout feature, ideal for relaxation and photography. The hotel is just 3.1 km from Dragon Bridge and 4 km from Han Market, making it suitable for both leisure and business travelers.

Tips for Choosing Hotels And Enjoying Da Nang to the Fullest

Best Time to Visit

The ideal time to visit Da Nang is March to September, with dry weather and sunshine perfect for beach activities. From October to February, cooler temperatures and fewer crowds create a more relaxed atmosphere.

Local Cuisine Highlights

  • Mi Quang – thick noodles with rich broth

  • Fish cake noodle soup (Bun Cha Ca)

  • Vietnamese pancakes (Banh Xeo)

  • Fresh seafood

  • Rice paper rolls with pork (Banh Trang Cuon Thit Heo)

Average meal cost ranges from 50,000 – 150,000 VND per person.

Transportation

  • Taxis & ride-hailing apps (Grab, Gojek)

  • Motorbike rentals (100,000–150,000 VND/day)

  • Public buses for budget travelers

Must Visit Attractions And Photo Spots

  • Golden Bridge (Ba Na Hills)

  • Marble Mountains

  • Son Tra Peninsula & Linh Ung Pagoda

  • Dragon Bridge

  • Hoi An Ancient Town

We hope these recommendations help you choose the perfect hotel for your stay in Da Nang. Whether you’re planning a short getaway or a long vacation, this vibrant coastal city always has something special to offer. Du Lich Viet wishes you a memorable and meaningful journey with family and friends.

posts.title: Top 10 Fascinating Destinations In Da Nang Travel Tour
posts.excerpt: Da Nang, widely known as the most livable city in Vietnam, is an ideal destination for the 2026 holiday season. From the charming My Khe Beach and the magical Ba Na Hills to the sacred Marble Mountain
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang, widely known as the most livable city in Vietnam, is an ideal destination for the 2026 holiday season. From the charming My Khe Beach and the magical Ba Na Hills to the sacred Marble Mountains and the ancient town of Hoi An, this coastal city offers a perfect blend of nature, culture, and modern attractions. This article highlights must-visit destinations and unique experiences to help travelers enjoy a memorable early-year vacation in Da Nang.

Da Nang has long been a favorite destination for both domestic and international visitors. Especially during the New Year holiday, it becomes an ideal place to explore thanks to its pleasant climate, diverse attractions, and vibrant atmosphere. From pristine beaches and world-class entertainment complexes to spiritual landmarks and cultural heritage sites, Da Nang promises unforgettable experiences for your 2026 getaway.

1. My Khe Beach – Where Happiness Begins

My Khe Beach, with its soft white sand stretching along the coastline and crystal-clear blue water, is not only one of the most beautiful beaches in the world as recognized by Forbes, but also a symbol of Da Nang tourism. Visiting My Khe during the New Year holiday allows travelers to enjoy fresh air and a peaceful atmosphere, far from the hustle and bustle of big cities.

Although it is not peak beach season, the weather remains pleasant with gentle sunshine, making it ideal for outdoor activities such as beach walks, light sports, or simply relaxing by the sea. Visitors can also enjoy fresh seafood at seaside restaurants, from casual local eateries to upscale dining venues. Early mornings at My Khe are especially beautiful, offering stunning sunrise views and perfect photo opportunities.

2. Ba Na Hills – A Fairytale Land Above The Clouds

Ba Na Hills, often referred to as “Heaven on Earth,” is a French-style resort complex located at an altitude of 1,489 meters above sea level. The world-record cable car system offers breathtaking views as it passes through clouds and lush forests.

During the New Year holiday, visitors can experience four seasons in one day, from cool mornings to chilly evenings. Highlights include the iconic Golden Bridge, the charming French Village, Le Jardin d’Amour flower gardens, the historic Debay Wine Cellar, and Linh Ung Pagoda. Fantasy Park offers hundreds of indoor games suitable for all ages. Booking tickets in advance is recommended during holiday periods.

3. Marble Mountains – A Legend Of Stone And Spirituality

The Marble Mountains, also known as Ngu Hanh Son, consist of five limestone hills representing the five elements. Located about eight kilometers from the city center, this site is both a natural wonder and a spiritual center with ancient caves, pagodas, and panoramic viewpoints.

Visitors can explore famous caves such as Huyen Khong Cave and Am Phu Cave, as well as Tam Thai Pagoda. Nearby, the Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village showcases over 400 years of traditional craftsmanship, offering beautifully carved marble sculptures and souvenirs.

4. Linh Ung Pagoda – A Sacred Symbol By The Sea

Located on the Son Tra Peninsula, Linh Ung Pagoda is home to the majestic 67-meter-tall Lady Buddha statue facing the sea. The pagoda offers a peaceful atmosphere, stunning coastal views, and a strong sense of spiritual tranquility.

It is an ideal place to pray for peace, admire Buddhist architecture, and enjoy panoramic views of Da Nang city and My Khe Beach. Visiting in the late afternoon allows travelers to witness a breathtaking sunset.

5. Asia Park – Asian-Standard Entertainment Park

Asia Park is a large entertainment complex showcasing the cultures of eleven Asian countries. It features thrilling rides, family-friendly attractions, cultural architecture, and Sun Wheel, one of the world’s tallest Ferris wheels.

The park is perfect for families and groups, offering cultural performances, diverse dining options, and exciting nighttime views of Da Nang.

6. Da Nang’s Iconic Bridges – Architectural Masterpieces

Known as the “City of Bridges,” Da Nang boasts unique architectural landmarks such as the Dragon Bridge, Han River Swing Bridge, Tran Thi Ly Bridge, and Thuan Phuoc Bridge.

Visitors can enjoy a Han River cruise at night to admire the illuminated skyline and watch the Dragon Bridge breathe fire and water on weekend evenings. The Love Bridge nearby is a popular romantic spot for couples.

7. Hai Van Pass – The World’s Most Scenic Coastal Road

Hai Van Pass, known as “The First Magnificent Pass Under Heaven,” is one of the most beautiful coastal mountain roads in the world. From its peak, travelers can enjoy panoramic views of Da Nang city, Lang Co Bay, and the surrounding mountains.

The cool climate and misty scenery during early-year months create a magical atmosphere, making it a favorite destination for adventure lovers and photographers.

8. Hoi An Ancient Town – A UNESCO World Heritage Site

Located about 30 kilometers from Da Nang, Hoi An Ancient Town is famous for its preserved architecture, lantern-lit streets, and rich cultural heritage. Walking through its narrow alleys, visiting ancient houses, Japanese Covered Bridge, and traditional assembly halls offers a glimpse into Vietnam’s trading past.

At night, the town glows with colorful lanterns and floating candle lights along the Hoai River. Local specialties such as Cao Lau, Mi Quang, and traditional pastries are must-try experiences.

9. Than Tai Hot Spring Park – Relaxation In Nature

Than Tai Hot Spring Park is a perfect place to unwind after days of sightseeing. Located in Hoa Vang District, this wellness destination offers natural hot mineral baths, mud baths, herbal baths, and Japanese-style onsen experiences.

Surrounded by mountains and greenery, it combines relaxation, health care, and entertainment, making it ideal for families and couples.

10. Cu Lao Cham – A Pristine Island Paradise

Cu Lao Cham, a UNESCO-recognized World Biosphere Reserve, is located about 15 kilometers off the coast of Hoi An. The island is known for its clear waters, diverse marine life, and unspoiled natural beauty.

Visitors can snorkel to explore coral reefs, relax on secluded beaches, visit ancient wells and temples, and enjoy freshly caught seafood. Environmental protection is strongly emphasized, creating a peaceful and eco-friendly travel experience.

Travel Tips For Da Nang New Year Holiday 2026

  • Plan and book flights, hotels, and tours early due to peak travel demand.

  • Consider guided tours for convenience and time efficiency.

  • Rent a motorbike or use taxis for flexible transportation.

  • Prepare light jackets for cooler evenings, especially in mountainous areas.

Da Nang is more than just a destination it is a complete travel experience where nature, culture, and modern life come together harmoniously. With these suggestions, your New Year holiday in 2026 promises to be truly memorable

posts.title: Discover Da Nang – The City Of Wonders
posts.excerpt: Da Nang in 2026 welcomes travelers with its vibrant energy and a harmonious blend of majestic nature and modern architecture. This article takes you on a journey to explore the city’s must-visit desti
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang in 2026 welcomes travelers with its vibrant energy and a harmonious blend of majestic nature and modern architecture. This article takes you on a journey to explore the city’s must-visit destinations from the lush Son Tra Peninsula and iconic bridges to the timeless charm of Hoi An Ancient Town along with memorable culinary experiences and convenient transportation options.

Located in central Vietnam, Da Nang has long been a favorite destination for both domestic and international travelers thanks to its beautiful beaches, spectacular landscapes, and distinctive architectural landmarks. Beyond its long stretches of white sand and turquoise waters, the city boasts a rich collection of natural attractions, cultural heritage sites, and historical landmarks. From green mountains and symbolic bridges to tranquil ancient streets, every corner of Da Nang tells its own story. This guide offers an in-depth look at the city’s highlights, including the latest travel updates for 2026.

1. Son Tra Peninsula – The Green Gem Of Da Nang

Known as the “green mountain” of Da Nang, Son Tra Peninsula is a breathtaking natural sanctuary featuring dramatic mountains, pristine beaches, and a rich biodiversity. Often referred to as the city’s “green lung,” it is also a protected nature reserve and home to the rare red-shanked douc langur one of the world’s most endangered primates, admired for its striking appearance. The best times to spot these animals are early morning or late afternoon.

One of the peninsula’s highlights is Linh Ung Pagoda at Bai But, home to the 67-meter-tall Lady Buddha statue facing the East Sea. From here, visitors can enjoy panoramic views of Da Nang city, My Khe Beach, and the distant Cham Islands. Ban Co Peak is another popular stop, offering fresh mountain air and sweeping views of both sea and forest. Adventure seekers can enjoy trekking, snorkeling, or relaxing at secluded beaches such as Bai Rang and Bai But. The ideal time to explore Son Tra is during the dry season, from March to September.

2. Da Nang Beaches – A Tropical Paradise

Da Nang is famous for its stunning coastline, with My Khe Beach standing out as the most iconic. Recognized by Forbes as one of the world’s most attractive beaches and praised by Lonely Planet for water sports, My Khe offers soft white sand, crystal-clear water, and a refreshing sea breeze. Visitors can swim, surf, parasail, or simply relax while enjoying fresh seafood at beachfront restaurants.

Other notable beaches include Non Nuoc Beach near the Marble Mountains, Thanh Binh Beach close to the city center, and Pham Van Dong Beach, popular among locals. These beaches are perfect for sunrise and sunset views and offer a peaceful escape from the city’s bustle.

3. Hoi An Ancient Town – Timeless Beauty And Cultural Heritage

Located less than 30 kilometers from Da Nang, Hoi An Ancient Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its well-preserved architecture and multicultural influences from Vietnam, Japan, China, and Europe. Moss-covered rooftops, narrow stone-paved alleys, and colorful lanterns create a romantic and nostalgic atmosphere.

Visitors can explore iconic landmarks such as the Japanese Covered Bridge, Fujian Assembly Hall, and Tan Ky Ancient House. Cultural experiences include lantern-making workshops, traditional tailoring, and cooking classes. At night, Hoi An becomes magical as lanterns illuminate the streets and boats carrying floating candles glide along the Hoai River.

4. Golden Bridge – A Masterpiece In The Clouds

Located within the Sun World Ba Na Hills complex, the Golden Bridge is one of Da Nang’s most iconic landmarks. Supported by two giant stone hands emerging from the mountainside, the golden walkway appears to float above the clouds. Since its opening in 2018, the bridge has gained global recognition and become a symbol of Vietnamese tourism.

Walking across the bridge offers breathtaking views of the Ba Na Mountains and the distant coastline. For the best experience, visit early in the morning or on weekdays to avoid crowds.

5. Han River Swing Bridge – A Symbol Of Innovation

The Han River Swing Bridge is the only swing bridge in Vietnam and a source of pride for Da Nang residents. Designed and built by Vietnamese engineers, the bridge rotates 90 degrees at night to allow ships to pass. This unique event usually takes place late at night and attracts both locals and visitors.

Watching the bridge rotate from a river cruise or a riverside café is a memorable experience and highlights the city’s creativity and modern spirit.

6. Dragon Bridge – Fire And Water Spectacle

Dragon Bridge is one of Da Nang’s most recognizable symbols. Designed in the shape of a dragon inspired by the Ly Dynasty, the bridge represents power and prosperity. Every Saturday and Sunday evening at 9:00 PM, the dragon breathes fire and sprays water, drawing large crowds and creating an unforgettable spectacle.

7. Linh Ung Pagoda – Where Spirituality Meets Nature

Linh Ung Pagoda on Son Tra Peninsula is one of three Linh Ung pagodas forming a spiritual triangle that protects the city. Nestled between the mountains and the sea, the pagoda offers a serene atmosphere and panoramic views. The towering Lady Buddha statue is the tallest of its kind in Vietnam and a symbol of peace and compassion.

8. Marble Mountains – A Sacred Natural Complex

The Marble Mountains, located about 8 kilometers from the city center, consist of five limestone hills named after the five elements. Thuy Son, the largest mountain, features impressive caves, ancient pagodas, and viewpoints overlooking the coast. At the base lies the Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village, famous for its traditional marble sculptures.

9. Da Nang Museum Of Cham Sculpture – A Gateway To Ancient Civilization

Established in 1915, the Museum of Cham Sculpture houses the world’s largest collection of Cham artifacts. With nearly 2,000 exhibits dating from the 5th to the 15th century, the museum offers deep insight into the art, religion, and culture of the ancient Champa Kingdom.

10. Asia Park – A World Of Colorful Entertainment

Asia Park is a modern amusement complex featuring thrilling rides, family-friendly attractions, and a cultural zone representing ten Asian countries. The highlight is the Sun Wheel, a 115-meter-tall Ferris wheel offering stunning nighttime views of Da Nang.

11. Da Nang Cuisine – A Journey Of Flavors

Da Nang is a culinary paradise where travelers can enjoy local specialties such as Mi Quang, fish cake noodle soup, banh xeo, nem lui, and Nam O fish salad. Street food markets and seaside eateries offer authentic flavors at affordable prices, making food exploration an essential part of any visit.

12. Transportation In Da Nang

Getting around Da Nang is easy and convenient. Motorbike rentals are popular for independent exploration, while taxis and ride-hailing services offer comfort and safety. Public buses provide a budget-friendly option for traveling between major attractions.

With its stunning landscapes, rich cultural heritage, modern infrastructure, and welcoming atmosphere, Da Nang is more than just a tourist destination it is a city full of inspiration. Whether you are a nature lover, a history enthusiast, or simply looking for relaxation, Da Nang promises unforgettable experiences and lasting memories.

posts.title: Top 5 Must See Festivals In Da Nang
posts.excerpt: Da Nang is not only famous for its stunning landscapes but also for its vibrant and distinctive cultural festivals. From the dazzling Da Nang International Fireworks Festival to the sacred Avalokitesv
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang is not only famous for its stunning landscapes but also for its vibrant and distinctive cultural festivals. From the dazzling Da Nang International Fireworks Festival to the sacred Avalokitesvara (Quan The Am) Festival, each event offers unforgettable experiences. Discover these remarkable festivals to make your Da Nang trip in 2026 even more memorable.

Da Nang, a beautiful and dynamic coastal city, is well known for its white-sand beaches, the fire-breathing Dragon Bridge, and exciting street food scene. Beyond these attractions, the city is also home to a wide range of unique cultural festivals that reflect strong local identity. These festivals are not only grand and lively but also provide visitors with a deeper understanding of local traditions, beliefs, and community spirit. Let’s explore the most special festivals that travelers should not miss when visiting Da Nang in 2026.

Overview Of Festival Culture In Da Nang

Da Nang is not only an important economic hub but also a rich cultural center where tradition and modernity blend harmoniously. Local festivals are more than entertainment events; they serve as a bond that connects the community, expresses respect toward deities and ancestors, and preserves valuable cultural heritage. From spiritual Buddhist festivals to large-scale international events, each celebration adds a unique color to Da Nang’s cultural landscape and attracts millions of visitors every year.

When people think of a Da Nang tour, they often focus on scenic attractions or diverse cuisine, overlooking the city’s vibrant festival life. These annual festivals offer fresh experiences and leave lasting impressions on travelers. Each festival tells its own story and contributes to the lively cultural identity of Da Nang.

Top Festivals For Tourists Visiting Da Nang

1. Da Nang International Fireworks Festival (DIFF)

The Da Nang International Fireworks Festival (DIFF) is one of the city’s most prominent international events, attracting millions of visitors every year. Usually held in summer and lasting about a month, the festival features spectacular fireworks performances by teams from around the world along the Han River. Each competition night transforms Da Nang’s skyline into a breathtaking display of light and color.

DIFF is more than a fireworks competition it is a series of cultural and artistic activities. Visitors can enjoy vibrant street festivals, live performances, food stalls, and romantic night views of the Han River. To secure the best experience, it is recommended to book tickets early, especially VIP grandstand seats or riverside restaurants and hotels. Ticket prices typically range from VND 400,000 to VND 2,000,000 depending on seating. The ideal time to visit is from late May to early July, when the weather is dry and pleasant.

Time: Usually June–July (official schedule announced in advance)
Location: Han River area, Da Nang, Vietnam

2. Avalokitesvara (Quan The Am) Festival At Marble Mountains

The Avalokitesvara Festival is one of the largest and most spiritually significant Buddhist festivals in Da Nang. It is held annually from the 19th to the 21st day of the second lunar month at the Marble Mountains complex. The festival is a time for Buddhists and visitors to pray for peace, prosperity, favorable weather, and happiness.

The festival includes two main parts: ceremonial rituals and festive activities. The ritual section features solemn ceremonies such as the procession of the Avalokitesvara statue, peace-praying rituals, and Dharma talks. The festive section is lively, with traditional folk games, chess competitions, lion dances, and cultural performances. Visitors can also release lanterns on the Co Co River as a symbol of hope and peace. There is no fixed entrance fee, aside from voluntary donations.

Time: 19th–21st day of the 2nd lunar month
Location: Marble Mountains, Da Nang, Vietnam

3. Da Nang Hot Air Balloon Festival

The Hot Air Balloon Festival is a relatively new event that has quickly gained popularity. Visitors can admire colorful hot air balloons floating across the blue sky, creating an impressive and photogenic scene. Adventurous travelers may even experience a balloon flight, enjoying panoramic views of Da Nang from above.

The festival usually takes place during major holidays and attracts photographers and exploration enthusiasts. Balloon flight experiences typically cost around VND 3,000,000–5,000,000 per short ride. Music, street food, and entertainment activities add to the festive atmosphere. Since balloon flights depend heavily on weather conditions, visitors should check forecasts in advance.

Time: Usually late April to early May
Location: Da Nang Hi-Tech Park and Hoa Trung Lake

4. Da Nang Music Festival

One of the most exciting cultural events in Da Nang is the Da Nang Music Festival, held periodically throughout the year to promote arts and showcase the city’s youthful and energetic image.

Visitors can enjoy a wide range of music genres, from traditional Vietnamese instruments and spontaneous street performances to modern concerts featuring well-known local and international artists. Stages are often set up along both sides of the Han River or at My Khe Beach, allowing guests to enjoy music while admiring the night scenery. Many performances are free or offered at affordable prices.

Time: Various times throughout the year, often on weekends or public holidays
Location: Han River area and central public spaces in Da Nang

5. Carnival Festival At Ba Na Hills

Ba Na Hills is one of Da Nang’s most iconic attractions, famous for its European-style architecture and cool climate. The Carnival Festival is a major highlight, bringing a lively and colorful atmosphere to the resort.

Professional dancers, often from Europe, perform in dazzling costumes inspired by global cultures. Street parades, energetic dances, and vibrant music create unforgettable moments. Performances take place multiple times daily at Du Dôme Square and the French Village. The festival is included in the Ba Na Hills entrance ticket, though visitors are advised to book cable car tickets early.

Time: Usually from April to September
Location: Du Dôme Square, French Village, Ba Na Hills, Da Nang

Tips For Enjoying Da Nang Festivals

  • Plan ahead: Major festivals like DIFF attract large crowds book flights, hotels, and tickets early.

  • Check schedules: Each festival has specific dates and locations.

  • Dress appropriately: Wear respectful clothing for spiritual festivals and comfortable outfits for outdoor events.

  • Protect personal belongings: Festivals can be crowded.

  • Try local food: Festival food stalls are a great way to experience Da Nang cuisine.

  • Respect local customs: Especially during traditional ceremonies.

  • Use public transport or taxis: Traffic can be heavy during festivals.

  • Carry some cash: Small vendors may not accept digital payments.

These are the most popular festivals that travelers to Da Nang truly love and should not miss. By experiencing these cultural celebrations, your journey to this vibrant coastal city will become even more meaningful and unforgettable in 2026.

posts.title: Top Must Visit Destinations When Traveling To Da Nang
posts.excerpt: Da Nang, often referred to as Vietnam’s most livable city, is an ideal destination for the New Year’s Day holiday 2026 thanks to its harmonious blend of spectacular natural landscapes and modern archi
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang, often referred to as Vietnam’s most livable city, is an ideal destination for the New Year’s Day holiday 2026 thanks to its harmonious blend of spectacular natural landscapes and modern architecture. From Ba Na Hills and the iconic Golden Bridge to My Khe Beach and the ancient town of Hoi An, visitors will enjoy unforgettable experiences enriched by distinctive local cuisine and vibrant cultural traditions.

During the New Year season, Da Nang becomes even more lively and enchanting as festive atmospheres fill the streets, beaches, and tourist attractions. If you are planning an early year getaway, explore the following highlights to make your New Year’s holiday in Da Nang truly memorable.

1. Ba Na Hills – A Fairyland Above The Clouds

Ba Na Hills is one of the most famous tourist complexes in Vietnam and a symbol of Da Nang tourism. Located about 25 kilometers west of the city center, Ba Na Hills sits atop Mount Chua at an altitude of 1,489 meters above sea level. One of its most unique features is the experience of four seasons in one day cool spring-like mornings, warm summer afternoons, gentle autumn evenings, and chilly winter nights.

Often described as a “miniature French village,” Ba Na Hills features European-style castles, spacious plazas, cobblestone streets, and romantic architecture. Every corner feels like a scene from a fairytale, making it a paradise for photography lovers. During the New Year holiday, the area is beautifully decorated and hosts various festive events, creating a vibrant and joyful atmosphere.

Visitors reach the summit by riding one of the world’s record-holding cable car systems. The ticket price ranges from approximately 800,000 to 900,000 VND per adult, including entrance and access to selected attractions at Fantasy Park. From the cable car, travelers can admire breathtaking views of the Truong Son Mountains, Da Nang city, and the stunning coastline.

2. Golden Bridge – An Iconic Architectural Masterpiece

Located within Ba Na Hills, the Golden Bridge has become one of Vietnam’s most recognizable landmarks. The pedestrian bridge stretches 148.6 meters long and is supported by two giant stone hands, creating the illusion of a golden ribbon floating above the clouds.

From the Golden Bridge, visitors can enjoy panoramic views of lush mountains, drifting clouds, and deep valleys below. It is one of the best places for unforgettable “check-in” photos in Da Nang. Although the bridge can be crowded during the New Year holiday, its spectacular design and surrounding scenery make it well worth the visit.

3. My Khe Beach – A Paradise Of White Sand And Blue Sea

My Khe Beach, recognized by Forbes as one of the most attractive beaches on the planet, is a must-visit destination in Da Nang. With its long stretch of fine white sand, crystal-clear water, and gentle waves, it is ideal for swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing by the sea.

The beach is free to access and well-equipped with tourist services. Visitors can enjoy activities such as swimming, surfing, parasailing, or simply walking along the shore at sunrise or sunset. Nearby seafood restaurants and beachfront cafés offer delicious local dishes and stunning ocean views. Even during the New Year holiday, Da Nang’s mild weather makes My Khe Beach an excellent place to unwind.

4. Son Tra Peninsula – The Green Lung Of Da Nang

Located about 10 kilometers from the city center, Son Tra Peninsula is often called the “green lung” of Da Nang. It features pristine forests, beautiful beaches, and a rich ecosystem.

Key attractions include Ban Co Peak with panoramic city views, Linh Ung Pagoda with the tallest Lady Buddha statue in Vietnam, and Mui Nghe one of the earliest sunrise spots in the city. Son Tra is also home to the rare red-shanked douc langur, considered the “queen” of the peninsula’s wildlife.

Visitors can also enjoy fresh seafood dishes such as squid, prawns, and shellfish prepared in traditional local styles.

5. Asia Park – A World-Class Entertainment Complex

Asia Park is one of the largest amusement parks in Southeast Asia, offering entertainment for visitors of all ages. The park is divided into three main zones: a cultural park representing ten Asian countries, an outdoor amusement area with thrilling rides, and a central entertainment zone.

The highlight is the Sun Wheel, one of the world’s tallest Ferris wheels, offering stunning nighttime views of Da Nang. Entrance tickets typically range from 100,000 to 150,000 VND, excluding individual rides.

6. Marble Mountains – A Spiritual And Mystical Landmark

The Marble Mountains, also known as Non Nuoc Mountains, consist of five limestone hills named after the five elements. Located about 7 kilometers from Da Nang city center, this site combines natural beauty with spiritual significance.

Thuy Son, the largest mountain, features impressive caves such as Huyen Khong Cave and Am Phu Cave, as well as ancient pagodas like Tam Thai and Linh Ung Pagoda. At the foot of the mountains lies the famous Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village, where visitors can purchase exquisite marble souvenirs.

7. Cu Lao Cham – A Peaceful Island Escape

Cu Lao Cham, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve located about 15 kilometers from Hoi An, offers pristine beaches, rich marine life, and a tranquil atmosphere. Visitors can swim, snorkel, dive, camp overnight, or enjoy fresh seafood such as squid, sea urchin, and abalone.

Speedboats from Cua Dai Port reach the island in 20–30 minutes, with round-trip tickets costing approximately 300,000–400,000 VND.

Travel And Accommodation Tips For New Year’s Holiday

Da Nang International Airport offers convenient domestic and international connections. Within the city, taxis, ride-hailing services, and motorbike rentals are popular options. Accommodation ranges from luxury beachfront resorts to budget-friendly homestays. Due to high demand during the New Year holiday, booking in advance is strongly recommended.

With its stunning landscapes, rich cultural heritage, exciting entertainment, and world-famous cuisine, Da Nang promises an unforgettable New Year’s holiday experience. Whether you seek relaxation, adventure, or cultural discovery, this vibrant coastal city offers something for every traveler welcoming the New Year 2026.

posts.title: Top 6 Famous Local Restaurants Every Traveler Should Try In Da Nang
posts.excerpt: Da Nang, often called the most livable city in Vietnam, captivates visitors not only with its stunning beaches and modern landmarks but also with its rich and diverse culinary scene. From humble stree
posts.contentHtml:
Da Nang, often called the most livable city in Vietnam, captivates visitors not only with its stunning beaches and modern landmarks but also with its rich and diverse culinary scene. From humble street food stalls to well-loved local eateries, Da Nang’s cuisine reflects the soul of Central Vietnam bold flavors, fresh ingredients, and deep cultural roots.

This guide introduces six iconic local restaurants that every traveler should experience when visiting Da Nang in 2026, along with helpful tips to make your food journey truly unforgettable.

Da Nang – A Culinary Paradise Of Central Vietnam

Da Nang is renowned for its pristine coastline, the iconic Dragon Bridge, and the dreamy Ba Na Hills. Beyond its scenic beauty, the city is a haven for food lovers. Da Nang cuisine represents a perfect balance between tradition and modernity, shaped by coastal life and Central Vietnam’s culinary heritage.

From flavorful breakfasts infused with seafood essence to late-night street snacks and hearty local dinners, every dish tells a story of local culture and hospitality. Below are some of the most famous food spots you should not miss.

1. Bun Mam Tran Ke Xuong – Bold And Authentic Local Flavors

Bun Mam (vermicelli with fermented fish sauce) is one of Da Nang’s most iconic dishes. At Tran Ke Xuong Restaurant, this dish reaches its finest form. A standard bowl includes crispy roasted pork, spring rolls, roasted peanuts, fresh herbs, and a signature fermented fish sauce prepared using a family recipe.

What makes this place special is the perfectly balanced sauce—savory, slightly sweet, aromatic, and never overpowering. The roasted pork is carefully selected to ensure crispy skin and tender meat. This restaurant has been serving locals for decades and remains a symbol of Da Nang’s traditional cuisine.

  • Price Range: 25,000–40,000 VND per bowl

  • Address: 23/14 Tran Ke Xuong Street, Hai Chau District

  • Opening Hours: 6:20 AM – 10:00 PM

2. Nam Hien Shrimp Pancakes – Crispy, Fresh, And Irresistible

Nam Hien is famous for its banh xeo tom nhay (crispy Vietnamese pancakes with fresh jumping shrimp). The pancake is thin and crunchy, filled with fresh shrimp, bean sprouts, minced pork, and scallions.

The highlight is the shrimp—added live into the sizzling pan to preserve natural sweetness. The pancakes are best enjoyed hot, wrapped in fresh herbs, and dipped into the restaurant’s signature dipping sauce, which is carefully crafted with liver paste for extra richness.

  • Price Range: 30,000–50,000 VND per serving

  • Address: 46 Phan Thanh Street, Thanh Khe District

  • Opening Hours: 10:00 AM – 9:30 PM

3. Cay Bang Snail Stall – A Beloved Street Food Experience

Cay Bang is one of Da Nang’s most popular street food spots, especially for snail lovers. The menu features a variety of snails such as rice snails, apple snails, and sea snails, cooked in different styles including lemongrass chili stir-fry, coconut stir-fry, or boiled with ginger dipping sauce.

The snails are flavorful, spicy, and aromatic, making them perfect for sharing with friends in the evening. Despite its casual sidewalk setting, the stall is clean, lively, and full of local character.

  • Price Range: 20,000–40,000 VND per plate

  • Atmosphere: Casual, open-air, vibrant street food vibe

4. Banh Dap Phan Chau Trinh – Simple Yet Refined

Banh Dap is a traditional Central Vietnamese dish made by layering crispy grilled rice paper with soft steamed rice sheets, then lightly pressing them together. At Phan Chau Trinh Street, this humble dish becomes a memorable culinary experience.

The dish is served with fermented fish sauce and can be ordered with dry toppings like fried shallots or richer versions with grilled pork or shrimp. Though simple, banh dap showcases the subtle sophistication of Da Nang’s food culture.

  • Price Range: 15,000–30,000 VND per serving

  • Address: 251 Phan Chau Trinh Street, Hai Chau District

  • Opening Hours: 9:00 AM – 9:00 PM

5. Quan Tran – A Complete Taste Of Da Nang Cuisine

Quan Tran offers a peaceful dining atmosphere away from the city’s bustle. The restaurant is known for presenting a wide range of Da Nang specialties in one place, making it ideal for first-time visitors.

Popular dishes include Quang noodles, steamed rice cakes, pork rolls with rice paper, bun mam, and banh dap. Each dish is prepared with attention to authenticity and traditional flavors.

  • Price Range: 30,000–80,000 VND per dish

  • Address: 4 Le Duan Street, Hai Chau District

  • Opening Hours: 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM

6. Ba Phien Fish Cake Noodle Soup – A Local Legend

Ba Phien Fish Cake Noodle Soup is one of the most famous eateries in Da Nang. The broth is light yet flavorful, simmered from fish bones and pumpkin, while the fish cakes are made fresh daily from high-quality fish.

A bowl typically includes both steamed and fried fish cakes, bamboo shoots, herbs, and crispy shallots. The restaurant has been family-run for generations and is deeply embedded in the city’s culinary heritage.

  • Price Range: 25,000–45,000 VND per bowl

  • Address: 63 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau District

  • Opening Hours: 6:00 AM – 10:30 PM

Tips For Exploring Da Nang’s Food Scene

  • Best Time To Visit: March to September offers dry weather, perfect for street food exploration.

  • Getting Around: Renting a motorbike allows easy access to hidden food spots.

  • Try Street Food: Do not miss snacks like rice paper cakes, grilled pork skewers, and sweet soups.

  • Carry Cash: Small local eateries often accept cash only.

  • Explore Local Markets: Con Market and Han Market are excellent for both food and cultural immersion.

  • Ask Locals: Da Nang residents are friendly and always happy to recommend great food spots.

With its vibrant street food culture and deeply rooted culinary traditions, Da Nang promises an unforgettable gastronomic journey. Exploring these six well-known eateries will give you an authentic taste of the city and enrich your travel experience in Central Vietnam.

posts.title: One Day Ninh Van Bay Nha Trang Tour
posts.excerpt: Ninh Van Bay Nha Trang is one of the most captivating coastal destinations in central Vietnam, renowned for its untouched beauty, crystal-clear waters, and peaceful atmosphere. This one-day Ninh Van B
posts.contentHtml:
Ninh Van Bay Nha Trang is one of the most captivating coastal destinations in central Vietnam, renowned for its untouched beauty, crystal-clear waters, and peaceful atmosphere. This one-day Ninh Van Bay travel guide for 2026 offers a comprehensive overview of how to get there, what to do, what to eat, and essential tips to help you enjoy a smooth and memorable journey.

Perfect for travelers seeking tranquility, nature, and unique marine experiences, Ninh Van Bay is an ideal escape from the bustling city life of Nha Trang.

Where Is Ninh Van Bay And What Makes It Special?

Ninh Van Bay is located on Hon Meo Peninsula, in Ninh Hoa District, Khanh Hoa Province, approximately 60 kilometers north of Nha Trang city. Unlike many other beaches in Nha Trang, Ninh Van Bay remains largely untouched by urban development, preserving its pristine coastline, soft white sand, vibrant coral reefs, and rich marine ecosystem.

What truly sets Ninh Van Bay apart is its serene and secluded atmosphere. Surrounded by mountains and the open sea, the bay offers a rare sense of privacy and harmony with nature. In the early morning, the bay is often covered in a gentle mist, creating a dreamlike and romantic landscape that leaves a lasting impression on visitors.

Often referred to as the “Maldives of Vietnam,” Ninh Van Bay is also home to exclusive eco-luxury resorts designed to blend seamlessly with the natural environment. Built using sustainable materials such as wood and bamboo, these resorts provide an ideal retreat for honeymooners, couples, and families seeking relaxation and comfort in a natural setting.

How To Get To Ninh Van Bay Nha Trang

There are two main ways to reach Ninh Van Bay: by speedboat or by road.

Traveling By Speedboat – Fast And Scenic

Taking a speedboat is the most convenient and time-saving option. From Nha Trang Port (Cau Da Port), the journey takes approximately 20–30 minutes. Ticket prices range from 150,000 to 250,000 VND per person per trip, depending on the boat and season.

Many travelers prefer booking a Nha Trang day tour package, which includes round-trip speedboat transfers, activities, and meals. It is highly recommended to book in advance, especially during peak travel seasons, to avoid long waiting times.

Traveling By Motorbike Or Car – A Flexible Adventure

For those who enjoy scenic road trips, traveling by motorbike or car is an excellent option. From Nha Trang city center, follow Tran Phu Bridge, continue along Pham Van Dong Street, and then head north on National Highway 1A. After approximately 36 kilometers, turn right at Ninh Da and continue toward Hyundai Port to reach Ninh Van Bay.

The coastal route offers breathtaking views of the sea and mountains, making it ideal for photography and short stops along the way. Motorbike rental costs around 100,000–150,000 VND per day, while car rental prices vary depending on vehicle type.

What To Do On A One-Day Ninh Van Bay Tour

A day at Ninh Van Bay promises unforgettable experiences, from underwater exploration to relaxing seaside activities.

Snorkeling And Diving To Explore Coral Reefs

Ninh Van Bay boasts a rich marine ecosystem with colorful coral reefs and diverse sea life. Snorkeling and scuba diving are must-try activities here. Visitors are provided with full equipment and guided by experienced instructors.

Beneath the clear waters, you will encounter vibrant corals, tropical fish, starfish, and other fascinating marine creatures. Snorkeling is suitable for beginners, while scuba diving offers a deeper exploration. Prices typically range from 300,000 to 500,000 VND, depending on the service.

Surfing And Paddleboarding For Adventure Lovers

For thrill-seekers, surfing and paddleboarding offer exciting ways to enjoy the sea. With gentle to moderate waves, Ninh Van Bay is suitable for both beginners and experienced surfers. Equipment rental and professional instruction are available, with prices starting from 200,000–400,000 VND per hour.

Fishing And Relaxing At Sea

If you prefer a slower pace, fishing on a boat in the calm waters of the bay is a peaceful and rewarding experience. Enjoy the fresh sea breeze while waiting for your catch. Many tours offer fishing combined with a freshly prepared seafood lunch on board.

Discover Hidden Beaches And Coastal Caves

Beyond the main beach, Ninh Van Bay features secluded beaches and small caves waiting to be explored. Kayaking or hiring a small boat allows you to reach these hidden spots, offering privacy and unique photo opportunities amid dramatic rock formations and lush greenery.

What To Eat On A One Day Ninh Van Bay Tour
